# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: '015'
  summary: Share temporary files and text with expiring links
  description: Provision Redis and create config.yaml in Configuration from the upstream example with private
    signing secrets, Redis URL, and public HTTPS address. Keep the app and worker on one host or shared storage.
  category: documents
  website: https://send.fudaoyuan.icu
  source: https://github.com/keven1024/015
  docs: https://github.com/keven1024/015#docker
  primary_service: '015'
  post_install: Provision Redis and create config.yaml in Configuration from the upstream example with private
    signing secrets, Redis URL, and public HTTPS address. Keep the app and worker on one host or shared storage.
  license: AGPL-3.0
  architectures:
  - amd64
  - arm64
  web:
    port: 80
  options:
    PORT:
      label: Published HTTP port
      help: Host-published port. The app listens on TCP port 80 inside Nex.
    CONFIG:
      label: Prepared 015 configuration
      help: Managed directory mounted at /nex-config. Choose storage readable by the application.
    UPLOADS:
      label: Shared uploaded files
      help: Managed directory mounted at /uploads. Choose storage writable by the application.
services:
  '015':
    image: docker.io/fudaoyuanicu/015-app:latest
    ports:
    - ${PORT:-23514}:80/tcp
    volumes:
    - ${CONFIG}:/nex-config:ro
    - ${UPLOADS}:/uploads
    entrypoint:
    - /bin/sh
    command:
    - -ec
    - |-
      test -r /nex-config/config.yaml
      ln -sf /nex-config/config.yaml /app/config.yaml
      exec /bin/sh /app/015.sh
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
  worker:
    image: docker.io/fudaoyuanicu/015-worker:latest
    volumes:
    - ${CONFIG}:/nex-config:ro
    - ${UPLOADS}:/uploads
    entrypoint:
    - /bin/sh
    command:
    - -ec
    - |-
      test -r /nex-config/config.yaml
      ln -sf /nex-config/config.yaml /config.yaml
      exec /bin/worker
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: 2FAuth
  summary: Manage one-time authentication codes in a web interface
  description: Use an HTTPS endpoint. Register the initial user on a trusted network, then disable registration
    in the app. Keep the application key with backups to decrypt stored tokens.
  category: security
  website: https://github.com/Bubka/2FAuth
  source: https://github.com/Bubka/2FAuth
  docs: https://docs.2fauth.app/getting-started/installation/docker/
  primary_service: 2fauth
  scalable: false
  license: AGPL-3.0
  web:
    port: 8000
  options:
    APP_KEY:
      label: Application key
      type: password
      help: 'Provide a Laravel application key with base64: followed by 32 encoded random bytes. Retain
        it for restores.'
    APP_URL:
      label: Public HTTPS URL
      help: Set the browser-facing address including https://.
    DATA:
      label: 2FAuth data
      help: User accounts, encryption data and stored 2FA entries.
    PORT:
      label: Web port
      help: Host-published TCP port. With a dedicated Primary network and host publishing off, use the
        application address on port 8000.
services:
  2fauth:
    image: docker.io/2fauth/2fauth:latest
    environment:
      APP_KEY: ${APP_KEY}
      APP_URL: ${APP_URL}
    volumes:
    - ${DATA}:/2fauth
    ports:
    - ${PORT:-8000}:8000/tcp
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: 7 Days to Die
  summary: Build and defend a shared world against zombie hordes
  description: >-
    Choose a client-reachable VLAN or private network as Primary network, and keep the folders on This host
    with one eligible x86-64 host. First boot downloads the dedicated server from Steam and prepares the world.
    From Join a Game, connect to the application's IPv4 address on port 26900 using the player password.
    Allow TCP 26900 and UDP 26900–26902 for players. Steam checks for updates on start. Back up the world
    folder with the app stopped before updating. This package starts a private vanilla PC server.
  category: games
  website: https://7daystodie.com/
  source: https://github.com/RunOnFlux/7dtd-server-flux
  docs: https://wiki.7d2d.net/hosting/
  license: Proprietary
  architectures: [amd64]
  tags:
    - survival
    - co-op
    - steam
  options:
    SERVER_NAME:
      label: Server name
    SERVER_PASSWORD:
      label: Player password
      type: password
    DATA:
      label: World and configuration
      help: Include this folder in stopped backups. It holds the saves, generated worlds, and server configuration.
    SERVER_FILES:
      label: Downloaded server files
      help: Steam can rebuild this folder. Allow space for the download and installation.
    MODS:
      label: Mods folder
      help: This folder can stay empty for vanilla play. Back it up if you add compatible mods.
services:
  7-days-to-die:
    image: docker.io/runonflux/7dtd-server-flux:latest
    expose:
      - "26900/tcp"
      - "26900/udp"
      - "26901/udp"
      - "26902/udp"
    environment:
      SDTD_ServerName: ${SERVER_NAME:-7 Days to Die}
      SDTD_ServerPassword: ${SERVER_PASSWORD}
      SDTD_ServerVisibility: "0"
      STEAM_BRANCH: public
      FLUX_CROSSPLAY: "false"
      FLUX_BACKUP_KEEP: "0"
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/mnt/7dtd/data
      - ${SERVER_FILES}:/mnt/7dtd/server
      - ${MODS}:/mnt/7dtd/mods
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: A Dark Room
  summary: Play the upstream browser-based text adventure
  description: Serves the upstream static game from a verified source revision. Each browser retains its own save.
  category: games
  source: https://github.com/doublespeakgames/adarkroom
  website: https://adarkroom.doublespeakgames.com/
  docs: https://github.com/doublespeakgames/adarkroom/blob/1fada4620b6c66bd07bf15a3f1eb8223df8bc1d7/README.md
  license: MPL-2.0
  primary_service: a-dark-room
  web:
    port: 80
  post_install: Choose a client-reachable primary network and open the app using its assigned address.
services:
  a-dark-room:
    image: docker.io/library/nginx:latest
    expose:
      - 80/tcp
    entrypoint: [/bin/sh, -ec]
    command:
      - |
        revision=1fada4620b6c66bd07bf15a3f1eb8223df8bc1d7
        file=$$(mktemp)
        trap 'rm -f "$$file"' EXIT
        curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' \
          --retry 2 --max-time 60 --max-filesize 12582912 \
          "https://codeload.github.com/doublespeakgames/adarkroom/tar.gz/$$revision" -o "$$file"
        printf '%s  %s\n' '9138920520c5268a6575cb68fe1487927138b998ca75d6764f2f88acbe9b0012' "$$file" | sha256sum -c -
        root="adarkroom-$$revision"
        tar -xzf "$$file" -C /usr/share/nginx/html --strip-components=1 \
          "$$root/LICENSE.md" "$$root/index.html" "$$root/browserWarning.html" "$$root/mobileWarning.html" \
          "$$root/favicon.ico" "$$root/audio" "$$root/css" "$$root/img" "$$root/lang" "$$root/lib" "$$root/script"
        test -s /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html
        rm -f "$$file"
        trap - EXIT
        exec /docker-entrypoint.sh nginx -g 'daemon off;'
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: Abiotic Factor
  summary: Run a co-op survival server in the GATE research facility
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Use the game’s server browser or the app’s Primary address on UDP 7777. The Steam query port is
    UDP 27015. SteamCMD installs the server on first boot and checks for updates on restart. Make
    a stopped backup before applying game updates.

  website: https://www.abioticfactor.com/
  source: https://github.com/indifferentbroccoli/abiotic-factor-server-docker
  docs: https://github.com/indifferentbroccoli/abiotic-factor-server-docker#readme
  license: Proprietary game server

    - amd64
  tags:
    - survival
    - multiplayer
  options:
    SERVER_NAME:
      label: Server name
      help: Name displayed in the game’s server browser.
    JOIN_PASSWORD:
      label: Join password
      type: password
      help: Choose a password and share it with your players.
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.

  abiotic-factor:

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: AdGuard Home
  summary: Filter ads and trackers through your own DNS server
  description: DNS filtering for your LAN. In Install, Network choose Primary network, a registered cluster VLAN
    reachable by your clients, then Fixed with an unused address/prefix and Default gateway. Leave Also publish
    ports on host addresses unchecked. After Install open http://APP-IP:3000, create the administrator, choose all
    DNS interfaces and web port 80; then use http://APP-IP/ for administration. Point router/client DNS to APP-IP
    on port 53, both TCP and UDP. The shared-network default alone cannot serve LAN DNS. DHCP and encrypted DNS
    are not configured. On Basics choose Runs on, Only these hosts and one host; keep state folders on This host.
    This keeps one copy on that host with no automatic failover. Use ACTIONS, Back up now with the stopped-copy
    option and select all state folders before updates.
  category: networking
  website: https://adguard.com/en/adguard-home/overview.html
  source: https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdGuardHome
  license: GPL-3.0
  scalable: false
  tags:
  - dns
  - ad-blocking
  - privacy
  options:
    SETUP_PORT:
      label: Initial setup port
      help: Only used when Also publish ports on host addresses is checked. For the required dedicated primary network
        leave that checkbox off and open http://APP-IP:3000 for first setup; select all DNS interfaces and web port
        80.
    PORT:
      label: Web port
      help: Only the optional host publication. With a registered cluster VLAN as Primary network and host publishing
        unchecked, use http://APP-IP/ after the first-run wizard. Configure LAN DNS clients to use APP-IP:53.
    WORK:
      label: DNS data
      help: Keep DNS data on This host. Nex creates /opt/adguardhome/work as persistent storage; no host folder
        setup is needed. Include this folder and Configuration together in a stopped Nex backup.
    CONFIG:
      label: Configuration
      help: Keep Configuration on This host. Nex creates /opt/adguardhome/conf; the wizard writes AdGuardHome.yaml
        and credentials. Include it with DNS data in a stopped Nex backup.
services:
  adguard-home:
    image: adguard/adguardhome:latest
    ports:
    - ${SETUP_PORT:-3003}:3000/tcp
    - ${PORT:-8082}:80/tcp
    expose:
    - 53/tcp
    - 53/udp
    volumes:
    - ${WORK}:/opt/adguardhome/work
    - ${CONFIG}:/opt/adguardhome/conf
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

  summary: Host multiplayer AssaultCube matches
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Use the matching 1.3.0.2 client and direct connect to the app’s Primary address on UDP 28763. UDP
    28764 serves information queries. This server starts unlisted. With the app stopped, use config/serverpwd.cfg
    in the managed folder to set a unique game administrator password and edit the map rotation in
    config/maprot.cfg.
  category: games
  website: https://assault.cubers.net/

  docs: https://assault.cubers.net/docs/server.html
  license: Zlib server code with separately licensed game media
  architectures:
  - amd64
  tags:
  - fps
  - multiplayer

    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  assaultcube:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/yolks:debian
    expose:
    - 28763/udp
    - 28764/udp
    volumes:
    - ${DATA}:/home/container
    user: 1000:1000
    command:
    - /bin/bash
    - -ec
    - |
      download() {
        local url="$$1" sha256="$$2" target="$$3"
        curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 "$$url" -o "$$target"
        printf '%s  %s\n' "$$sha256" "$$target" | sha256sum --check --status || {
          echo "The server download did not match the release checksum." >&2
          return 1
        }
      }


      cd "$$HOME"
      if [ ! -x ./bin_unix/linux_64_server ]; then
        staging=$$(mktemp -d ./.assaultcube-install.XXXXXX)
        trap 'rm -rf "$$staging"' EXIT
        download https://github.com/assaultcube/AC/releases/download/v1.3.0.2/AssaultCube_v1.3.0.2_LockdownEdition_RC1.tar.bz2 \
          9b3118e7929253f0114fa06cad8310faab646d177b4660406011152f34086b55 "$$staging/release.tar.bz2"
        mkdir -p "$$staging/files" bin_unix
        tar -xjf "$$staging/release.tar.bz2" -C "$$staging/files" ./bin_unix/linux_64_server ./config ./packages
        cp -Rn "$$staging/files/config" "$$staging/files/packages" ./
        chmod 755 "$$staging/files/bin_unix/linux_64_server"
        mv "$$staging/files/bin_unix/linux_64_server" ./bin_unix/linux_64_server
        rm -rf "$$staging"
        trap - EXIT
      fi
      exec ./bin_unix/linux_64_server -f28763 -mlocalhost
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

  astro-colony:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/steamcmd:debian
    environment:
      SERVER_NAME: ${SERVER_NAME:-Nex Astro Colony}
    expose:
    - 7777/udp
    - 27015/udp
    volumes:
    - ${DATA}:/home/container
    command:
    - /bin/bash
    - -ec
    - |
      # SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
      # Embedded in catalogue manifests that install a server through SteamCMD.
      # A package passes a dedicated-server app ID and either linux or windows.
      nex_steamcmd_update() {
        local app_id="$$1" platform="$$2"
        local archive attempt architecture steamclient
        local -a update=(+@ShutdownOnFailedCommand 1 +@NoPromptForPassword 1)

        cd "$$HOME"
        mkdir -p steamcmd serverfiles
        if [[ ! -x steamcmd/steamcmd.sh ]]; then
          archive=$$(mktemp)
          if ! curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \
            https://media.steampowered.com/client/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz -o "$$archive" \
            || ! tar -xzf "$$archive" -C steamcmd; then
            rm -f "$$archive"
            return 1
          fi
          rm -f "$$archive"
        fi

        if [[ "$$platform" == windows ]]; then
          update+=(+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows)
        fi
        update+=(+force_install_dir "$$HOME/serverfiles" +login anonymous +app_update "$$app_id" +quit)

        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          if ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh "$${update[@]}"; then
            break
          fi
          if [[ "$$attempt" == 3 ]]; then
            return 1
          fi
          sleep "$$((attempt * 5))"
        done

        for architecture in 32 64; do
          steamclient="$$HOME/steamcmd/linux$$architecture/steamclient.so"
          if [[ -f "$$steamclient" ]]; then
            mkdir -p ".steam/sdk$$architecture"
            ln -sfn "$$steamclient" ".steam/sdk$$architecture/steamclient.so"
          fi
        done
        cd serverfiles
      }

      nex_steamcmd_update 2934900 linux
      exec ./AstroColony/Binaries/Linux/AstroColonyServer -log -QueryPort=27015 "-SteamServerName=$$SERVER_NAME"
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: 'BATTALION: Legacy'
  summary: 'Host a BATTALION: Legacy multiplayer match'
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Join the app’s Primary address on UDP 7777. The Steam server query port is UDP 27015. Keep your
    administrator password private. First boot downloads the server through SteamCMD. Restarts check
    for updates. Make a stopped backup before applying game updates.
  category: games
  website: https://store.steampowered.com/app/489940/
  source: https://github.com/nexvirtualization/nex-catalogue/tree/main/apps/battalion-legacy
  docs: https://steamcommunity.com/app/489940/discussions/0/3432326055078758588/
  license: Proprietary game server
  architectures:
  - amd64
  tags:
  - steam
  - fps
  options:
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
    SERVER_NAME:
      label: Server name
      help: Name shown to players in the server browser.
    ADMIN_PASSWORD:
      label: Administrator password
      help: Use Generate for a unique administrator password.
      type: password
services:
  battalion-legacy:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/steamcmd:debian
    environment:
      SERVER_NAME: ${SERVER_NAME:-Nex BATTALION}
      ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${ADMIN_PASSWORD}
    expose:
    - 7777/udp
    - 27015/udp
    volumes:
    - ${DATA}:/home/container
    command:
    - /bin/bash
    - -ec
    - |
      # SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
      # Embedded in catalogue manifests that install a server through SteamCMD.
      # A package passes a dedicated-server app ID and either linux or windows.
      nex_steamcmd_update() {
        local app_id="$$1" platform="$$2"
        local archive attempt architecture steamclient
        local -a update=(+@ShutdownOnFailedCommand 1 +@NoPromptForPassword 1)

        cd "$$HOME"
        mkdir -p steamcmd serverfiles
        if [[ ! -x steamcmd/steamcmd.sh ]]; then
          archive=$$(mktemp)
          if ! curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \
            https://media.steampowered.com/client/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz -o "$$archive" \
            || ! tar -xzf "$$archive" -C steamcmd; then
            rm -f "$$archive"
            return 1
          fi
          rm -f "$$archive"
        fi

        if [[ "$$platform" == windows ]]; then
          update+=(+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows)
        fi
        update+=(+force_install_dir "$$HOME/serverfiles" +login anonymous +app_update "$$app_id" +quit)

        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          if ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh "$${update[@]}"; then
            break
          fi
          if [[ "$$attempt" == 3 ]]; then
            return 1
          fi
          sleep "$$((attempt * 5))"
        done

        for architecture in 32 64; do
          steamclient="$$HOME/steamcmd/linux$$architecture/steamclient.so"
          if [[ -f "$$steamclient" ]]; then
            mkdir -p ".steam/sdk$$architecture"
            ln -sfn "$$steamclient" ".steam/sdk$$architecture/steamclient.so"
          fi
        done
        cd serverfiles
      }

      nex_steamcmd_update 805140 linux
      exec ./Battalion/Binaries/Linux/BattalionServer-Linux-Shipping Battalion -Port=7777 -QueryPort=27015 \
        "-SteamServerName=$$SERVER_NAME" -Queue=Wartide "-AdminPassword=$$ADMIN_PASSWORD" -Log
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: BookLogr
  summary: Track books, reading progress and notes
  description: Runs the BookLogr web interface and SQLite API behind a shared address. Use the same
    public URL for the browser and the application's Web address option.
  category: productivity
  website: https://github.com/Mozzo1000/booklogr
  source: https://github.com/Mozzo1000/booklogr
  docs: https://github.com/Mozzo1000/booklogr/wiki/Install-with-Docker
  license: Apache-2.0
  architectures: [amd64, arm64]
  primary_service: booklogr
  web:
    port: 80
  options:
    WEB_ADDRESS:
      label: Web address
      help: Required absolute browser URL, including scheme and port, without a path. Use the HTTPS
        reverse-proxy address when exposing the app publicly.
    AUTH_SECRET:
      label: Signing secret
      help: Enter a long, randomly generated value for session token signing. Keep it stable.
      type: password
    OWNER_EMAIL:
      label: Initial account email
      help: Email of the first local account. Public registration is disabled.
    OWNER_PASSWORD:
      label: Initial account password
      help: Choose a strong unique password for the first local account.
      type: password
    DATA:
      label: Database
      help: Use a writable folder on This host for the SQLite database. Back up this folder.
    PORT:
      label: Web port
      help: Host-published HTTP port when host publishing is enabled.
services:
  booklogr:
    image: docker.io/library/caddy:latest
    entrypoint: [/bin/sh, -ec]
    command:
      - |
        caddy run --config - --adapter caddyfile <<'CADDYFILE'
        {
          auto_https off
        }
        :80 {
          @api path /v1 /v1/*
          reverse_proxy @api backend:5000
          reverse_proxy web:80
        }
        CADDYFILE
    ports:
      - ${PORT:-23389}:80/tcp
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
  web:
    image: docker.io/mozzo/booklogr-web:v1.12.0
    environment:
      BL_API_ENDPOINT: ${WEB_ADDRESS}
      BL_ALLOW_REGISTRATION: "false"
      BL_DEMO_MODE: "false"
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
  backend:
    image: docker.io/mozzo/booklogr:v1.12.0
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: sqlite:///books.db
      AUTH_SECRET_KEY: ${AUTH_SECRET}
      AUTH_ALLOW_REGISTRATION: "False"
      AUTH_REQUIRE_VERIFICATION: "False"
      AUTH_DEFAULT_USER: ${OWNER_EMAIL}
      AUTH_DEFAULT_PASSWORD: ${OWNER_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/app/instance
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

    - |
      # SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
      # Embedded in catalogue manifests that install a server through SteamCMD.
      # A package passes a dedicated-server app ID and either linux or windows.
      nex_steamcmd_update() {
        local app_id="$$1" platform="$$2"
        local archive attempt architecture steamclient
        local -a update=(+@ShutdownOnFailedCommand 1 +@NoPromptForPassword 1)

        cd "$$HOME"
        mkdir -p steamcmd serverfiles
        if [[ ! -x steamcmd/steamcmd.sh ]]; then
          archive=$$(mktemp)
          if ! curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \
            https://media.steampowered.com/client/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz -o "$$archive" \
            || ! tar -xzf "$$archive" -C steamcmd; then
            rm -f "$$archive"
            return 1
          fi
          rm -f "$$archive"
        fi

        if [[ "$$platform" == windows ]]; then
          update+=(+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows)
        fi
        update+=(+force_install_dir "$$HOME/serverfiles" +login anonymous +app_update "$$app_id" +quit)

        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          if ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh "$${update[@]}"; then
            break
          fi
          if [[ "$$attempt" == 3 ]]; then
            return 1
          fi
          sleep "$$((attempt * 5))"
        done

        for architecture in 32 64; do
          steamclient="$$HOME/steamcmd/linux$$architecture/steamclient.so"
          if [[ -f "$$steamclient" ]]; then
            mkdir -p ".steam/sdk$$architecture"
            ln -sfn "$$steamclient" ".steam/sdk$$architecture/steamclient.so"
          fi
        done
        cd serverfiles
      }

      nex_steamcmd_update 3017590 linux
      mkdir -p "$$HOME/brickadia"
      exec ./Brickadia/Binaries/Linux/BrickadiaServer-Linux-Shipping -server -log -port=7777 \
        "-UserDir=$$HOME/brickadia" "-token=$$HOSTING_TOKEN"
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

  name: ClassiCube MCGalaxy
  summary: Host a persistent ClassiCube building world
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Use Direct connect in the ClassiCube client and enter the app’s Primary address on TCP 25565. First
    boot downloads the official MCGalaxy Linux-compatible release. The server starts unlisted. Stop
    the app to edit properties/server.properties and manage world files or player ranks.
  category: games
  website: https://www.classicube.net/
  source: https://github.com/ClassiCube/MCGalaxy
  docs: https://github.com/ClassiCube/MCGalaxy#readme
  license: ClassiCube MCGalaxy server
  architectures:
  - amd64
  tags:
  - sandbox
  - multiplayer
  options:
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  classicube-mcgalaxy:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/yolks:mono_latest
    expose:
    - 25565/tcp
    volumes:
    - ${DATA}:/home/container
    user: 1000:1000
    command:
    - /bin/bash
    - -ec
    - |
      download() {
        local url="$$1" sha256="$$2" target="$$3"
        curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 "$$url" -o "$$target"
        printf '%s  %s\n' "$$sha256" "$$target" | sha256sum --check --status || {
          echo "The server download did not match the release checksum." >&2
          return 1
        }
      }


      cd "$$HOME"
      if [ ! -f ./mcgalaxy/MCGalaxyCLI.exe ]; then
        staging=$$(mktemp -d ./.mcgalaxy-install.XXXXXX)
        trap 'rm -rf "$$staging"' EXIT
        download https://cdn.classicube.net/client/mcg/release/MCGalaxy.zip \
          d65f48af9875fabce15568d836860239e2ee3b041f829759e24b78491b2dfb9d "$$staging/release.zip"
        unzip -oq "$$staging/release.zip" -d "$$staging"
        mv "$$staging/MCGalaxy" ./mcgalaxy
        rm -rf "$$staging"
        trap - EXIT
      fi
      mkdir -p properties
      if [ ! -f properties/server.properties ]; then
        printf 'server-name = Nex ClassiCube\npublic = false\nport = 25565\n' > properties/server.properties
      fi
      exec mono ./mcgalaxy/MCGalaxyCLI.exe
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

        echo "Accept the Clone Hero EULA in Nex before starting." >&2
        exit 1

    initial administrator key using the backend container and enter it in the dashboard. Back up Data and
    retain the instance secret.
  architectures:
  - amd64
  - arm64
  web:
    port: 6791
  options:
    API_URL:
      label: Api url
      help: Enter the deployment value described in the upstream setup guide.
    ACTIONS_URL:
      label: Actions url
      help: Enter the deployment value described in the upstream setup guide.
    INSTANCE_SECRET:
      label: Instance secret
      help: Use the credential or secret required by the upstream configuration.
      type: password
    PORT:
      label: Published HTTP port
      help: Host-published port. The app listens on TCP port 6791 inside Nex.
    API_PORT:
      label: Published public API port
      help: Host-published port for the internal 3210/tcp endpoint.
    ACTIONS_PORT:
      label: Published HTTP actions port
      help: Host-published port for the internal 3211/tcp endpoint.
    DATA:
      label: Convex data
      help: Managed directory mounted at /convex/data. Choose storage writable by the backend.
services:
  convex:
    image: docker.io/library/caddy:latest
    ports:
    - ${PORT:-23513}:6791/tcp
    - ${API_PORT:-24513}:3210/tcp
    - ${ACTIONS_PORT:-25513}:3211/tcp
    entrypoint:
    - /bin/sh
    command:
    - -ec
    - |-
      printf '%s\n' '{
        auto_https off
      }
      :6791 {
        reverse_proxy dashboard:6791
      }
      :3210 {
        reverse_proxy backend:3210
      }
      :3211 {
        reverse_proxy backend:3211
      }' | exec caddy run --config - --adapter caddyfile
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
  backend:
    image: ghcr.io/convex/convex-backend:latest
    environment:
      CONVEX_CLOUD_ORIGIN: ${API_URL}
      CONVEX_SITE_ORIGIN: ${ACTIONS_URL}
      INSTANCE_SECRET: ${INSTANCE_SECRET}
      DISABLE_BEACON: 'true'

x-nex:
  name: CS2D
  summary: Host top-down tactical multiplayer matches
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Use a matching CS2D 1.0.1.8 client and connect to the app’s Primary address on UDP 36963. The first
    start installs the publisher’s dedicated binary and game data. Edit sys/server.cfg and add custom
    maps in the managed folder.
  category: games
  website: https://www.cs2d.com/
  source: https://www.cs2d.com/download.php
  docs: https://www.cs2d.com/serverhosting.php
  license: Proprietary game server
  architectures:
  - amd64
  tags:
  - shooter
  - multiplayer
  options:
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  cs2d:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/yolks:debian
    expose:
    - 36963/udp
    volumes:
    - ${DATA}:/home/container
    user: 1000:1000
    command:
    - /bin/bash
    - -ec
    - |
      download() {
        local url="$$1" sha256="$$2" target="$$3"
        curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 "$$url" -o "$$target"
        printf '%s  %s\n' "$$sha256" "$$target" | sha256sum --check --status || {
          echo "The server download did not match the release checksum." >&2
          return 1
        }
      }


      cd "$$HOME"
      if [ ! -x ./cs2d_dedicated ]; then
        staging=$$(mktemp -d ./.cs2d-install.XXXXXX)
        trap 'rm -rf "$$staging"' EXIT
        download 'https://www.unrealsoftware.de/get.php?get=cs2d_1018_linux.zip&p=1&cid=1225' \
          855314b79c1cca60e93834461784882464fe00bf6a5aa2e86017c4ecbc4b16b1 "$$staging/data.zip"
        download https://www.unrealsoftware.de/files_pub/cs2d_dedicated_linux.zip \
          a1b39e1f0aaca1903dc150dd9dfbfe67fcae67a264de56c3de1a7ba3b20ca7b0 "$$staging/server.zip"
        unzip -oq "$$staging/data.zip" -d "$$staging/files"
        unzip -p "$$staging/server.zip" cs2d_dedicated > "$$staging/cs2d_dedicated"
        cp -Rn "$$staging/files/." ./
        chmod 755 "$$staging/cs2d_dedicated"
        mv "$$staging/cs2d_dedicated" ./cs2d_dedicated
        rm -rf "$$staging"
        trap - EXIT
      fi
      exec ./cs2d_dedicated
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

x-nex:
  name: DDNet
  summary: Host cooperative DDrace maps
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    In the DDNet server browser, direct connect to the app’s Primary address on UDP 8303. The image
    downloads DDNet on first boot. Use your Nex administrator password for the remote console in-game.
    Stop the app before editing autoexec.cfg and storing custom maps in the managed folder.
  category: games
  website: https://ddnet.org/
  source: https://github.com/ich777/docker-ddnet-server
  docs: https://ddnet.org/settingscommands/
  license: Zlib game server
  architectures:
  - amd64
  tags:
  - multiplayer
  options:
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
    ADMIN_PASSWORD:
      label: Administrator password
      help: Use Generate for at least 12 letters or numbers.
      type: password
services:
  ddnet:
    image: ghcr.io/ich777/ddnetserver:latest
    environment:
      UID: '1000'
      GID: '1000'
      UMASK: '027'
      ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${ADMIN_PASSWORD}
    expose:
    - 8303/udp
    volumes:
    - ${DATA}:/serverdata/serverfiles
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    entrypoint:
    - /bin/bash
    - -ec
    - |
      [[ "$$ADMIN_PASSWORD" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9]{12,}$$ ]] || {
        echo "Use at least 12 letters or numbers for the DDNet administrator password." >&2
        exit 1
      }
      umask 077
      config=/serverdata/serverfiles/autoexec.cfg
      tmp=$$(mktemp /serverdata/serverfiles/autoexec.cfg.XXXXXX)
      if [ -f "$$config" ]; then
        awk '$$1 !~ /^(sv_port|sv_rcon_password|sv_rcon_mod_password|sv_rcon_helper_password)$$/' "$$config" > "$$tmp"
      else
        printf 'sv_name "Nex DDNet"\nsv_map "Sunny Side Up"\nsv_register 0\n' > "$$tmp"
      fi
      printf '\nsv_port 8303\nsv_rcon_password "%s"\n' "$$ADMIN_PASSWORD" >> "$$tmp"
      mv "$$tmp" "$$config"
      unset ADMIN_PASSWORD
      exec /opt/scripts/start.sh

  description: >-

      label: Registry password file
      help: Choose a protected cluster share containing a file named htpasswd with bcrypt credentials. Generate
        or update it with htpasswd -B. Restart all copies after changes.
    S3_BUCKET:
      label: S3 bucket
      help: Create a private bucket first. Use a dedicated bucket for each registry.
    S3_REGION:
      label: S3 region
      help: Region of the bucket, for example ap-southeast-2.
    S3_ENDPOINT:
      label: Custom S3 endpoint
      help: Optional HTTPS endpoint for a self-hosted S3-compatible service. Leave blank for AWS S3.

    Choose a client-reachable VLAN or private network as Primary network, and keep both folders on This host
    with one eligible x86-64 host. First boot authenticates with Strange Loop Games and generates a world.
    In Your Worlds, choose Add Server and enter the application's IPv4 address on UDP 3000. The map is
    available on TCP 3001. The world is unlisted and requires the player password. Back up both folders
    with the app stopped before updating the image.
  category: games
  website: https://play.eco/
  source: https://hub.docker.com/r/strangeloopgames/eco-game-server
  docs: https://wiki.play.eco/en/Server_on_Linux
  license: Proprietary
  architectures: [amd64]
  tags:
    - simulation
    - co-op
  options:
    SERVER_NAME:
      label: Server name
    SERVER_PASSWORD:
      label: Player password
      type: password
      help: Share this password with players. The account token is only for the server.
    ECO_TOKEN:
      label: Strange Loop Games account token
      type: password
      help: Copy a user token from the Account page at play.eco. Nex Generate does not create a valid Eco token.
    DATA:
      label: World saves
      help: Include this folder and Configuration in stopped backups.
    CONFIG:
      label: Configuration
      help: Nex applies the name, player password, and private networking settings on startup.
services:
  eco:
    image: docker.io/strangeloopgames/eco-game-server:latest
    expose:
      - "3000/udp"
      - "3001/tcp"
    entrypoint: [/bin/sh, -ec]
    command:
      - |
        umask 077
        config=/app/Configs/Network.eco
        input="$$config"
        if [ ! -f "$$input" ]; then
          input="$$config.template"
        fi
        next="$$(mktemp /app/Configs/Network.eco.XXXXXX)"
        trap 'rm -f "$$next"' EXIT
        jq --arg name "$$ECO_NAME" --arg password "$$ECO_SERVER_PASSWORD" \
          '.Name = $$name | .Password = $$password | .PublicServer = false | .UPnPEnabled = false | .RconIPAddress = "127.0.0.1"' \
          "$$input" > "$$next"
        mv "$$next" "$$config"
        exec /app/EcoServer --nogui "--userToken=$$ECO_USER_TOKEN"
    environment:
      ECO_NAME: ${SERVER_NAME:-Eco}
      ECO_SERVER_PASSWORD: ${SERVER_PASSWORD}
      ECO_USER_TOKEN: ${ECO_TOKEN}
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/app/Storage
      - ${CONFIG}:/app/Configs
    stop_grace_period: 120s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

x-nex:
  name: Factorio
  summary: Build a factory together in a private Factorio world
  description: >-
    Run one copy on a selected host and keep game data on This host. In Network, choose a cluster
    VLAN or routed private network reachable by players. In Factorio, use Multiplayer, Connect
    to address, and enter the app's Primary address on UDP 34197. Restrict the authenticated
    admin console on TCP 27015 to administrators. First startup creates a world.
    Use a matching client version and make a stopped backup before updating.
  category: games
  website: https://www.factorio.com/download
  source: https://github.com/factoriotools/factorio-docker
  docs: https://github.com/factoriotools/factorio-docker#readme
  license: Proprietary game server (MIT container)
  architectures: [amd64, arm64]
  tags: [automation, factory, multiplayer]
  options:
    GAME_PASSWORD:
      label: Join password
      type: password
      help: Set a password for players. Edit this setting in Nex and restart to change it.
    DATA:
      label: Saves, mods and settings
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in a stopped backup.
services:
  factorio:
    image: docker.io/factoriotools/factorio:stable
    environment:
      GAME_PASSWORD: ${GAME_PASSWORD}
    entrypoint:
      - /bin/sh
      - -ec
      - |
        config=/factorio/config/server-settings.json
        mkdir -p /factorio/config
        if [ ! -f "$$config" ]; then
          jq '.visibility.public = false | .visibility.lan = false' /opt/factorio/data/server-settings.example.json > "$$config"
        fi
        jq '.game_password = env.GAME_PASSWORD' "$$config" > "$$config.tmp"
        mv "$$config.tmp" "$$config"
        # Keep the image's Bash trace from logging its generated RCON password.
        export BASH_XTRACEFD=7
        exec /docker-entrypoint.sh 7>/dev/null
    expose:
      - "34197/udp"
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/factorio
    stop_grace_period: 60s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

x-nex:
  name: FiveM
  summary: Host a scripted Grand Theft Auto V multiplayer server
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Create a server registration key at the Cfx.re Portal before installing. In FiveM, direct connect
    to the app’s Primary address on port 30120. The first boot installs the basic game mode and creates
    server.cfg. Edit your configuration and resources in the managed folder with the app stopped.
  category: games
  website: https://fivem.net/
  source: https://github.com/spritsail/fivem
  docs: https://docs.fivem.net/docs/server-manual/setting-up-a-server-vanilla/
  license: Proprietary game server
  architectures:
  - amd64
  tags:
  - sandbox
  - multiplayer
  options:
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
    LICENSE_KEY:
      label: Cfx.re registration key
      help: Create your key at https://portal.cfx.re/servers/registration-keys.
      type: password
services:
  fivem:
    image: docker.io/spritsail/fivem:latest
    environment:
      LICENSE_KEY: ${LICENSE_KEY}
    expose:
    - 30120/tcp
    - 30120/udp
    volumes:
    - ${DATA}:/config
    entrypoint:
    - /sbin/tini
    - -g
    - --
    - /bin/sh
    - -ec
    - |
      case "$$LICENSE_KEY" in
        ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_-]*)
          echo "Enter a valid Cfx.re server registration key in Settings." >&2
          exit 1 ;;
      esac
      if [ ! -f /config/server.cfg ]; then
        cp -R /opt/cfx-server-data/resources /config/
        tmp=$$(mktemp /config/server.cfg.XXXXXX)
        cat > "$$tmp" <<'EOF'
      endpoint_add_tcp "0.0.0.0:30120"
      endpoint_add_udp "0.0.0.0:30120"
      sv_hostname "Nex FiveM"
      sets sv_projectName "Nex FiveM"
      sets sv_projectDesc "FiveM multiplayer"
      sv_scriptHookAllowed 0
      sv_maxclients 32
      sv_master1 ""
      ensure mapmanager
      ensure chat
      ensure spawnmanager
      ensure basic-gamemode
      EOF
        mv "$$tmp" /config/server.cfg
      fi
      exec /usr/bin/entrypoint
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: 'Holdfast: Nations At War'
  summary: Host custom battles and map rotations
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    In the server browser use Join Custom Server and enter the app’s Primary address on UDP 20100.
    Steam uses UDP 27000 for queries and UDP 8700 for communications. Edit serverfiles/serverconfig_nex.txt
    in the managed folder to customize the map rotation. First boot downloads the server through SteamCMD.
    Restarts check for updates. Make a stopped backup before applying game updates.
  category: games
  website: https://store.steampowered.com/app/589290/
  source: https://github.com/nexvirtualization/nex-catalogue/tree/main/apps/holdfast
  docs: https://wiki.holdfastgame.com/index.php?title=Server_Hosting
  license: Proprietary game server
  architectures:
  - amd64
  tags:
  - steam
  - multiplayer
  options:
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
    ADMIN_PASSWORD:
      label: Administrator password
      help: Use at least 12 letters, numbers, underscores or hyphens.
      type: password
services:
  holdfast:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/steamcmd:debian
    environment:
      ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${ADMIN_PASSWORD}
    expose:
    - 20100/udp
    - 27000/udp
    - 8700/udp
    volumes:
    - ${DATA}:/home/container
    command:
    - /bin/bash
    - -ec
    - |
      # SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
      # Embedded in catalogue manifests that install a server through SteamCMD.
      # A package passes a dedicated-server app ID and either linux or windows.
      nex_steamcmd_update() {
        local app_id="$$1" platform="$$2"
        local archive attempt architecture steamclient
        local -a update=(+@ShutdownOnFailedCommand 1 +@NoPromptForPassword 1)

        cd "$$HOME"
        mkdir -p steamcmd serverfiles
        if [[ ! -x steamcmd/steamcmd.sh ]]; then
          archive=$$(mktemp)
          if ! curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \
            https://media.steampowered.com/client/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz -o "$$archive" \
            || ! tar -xzf "$$archive" -C steamcmd; then
            rm -f "$$archive"
            return 1
          fi
          rm -f "$$archive"
        fi

        if [[ "$$platform" == windows ]]; then
          update+=(+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows)
        fi
        update+=(+force_install_dir "$$HOME/serverfiles" +login anonymous +app_update "$$app_id" +quit)

        for attempt in 1 2 3; do
          if ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh "$${update[@]}"; then
            break
          fi
          if [[ "$$attempt" == 3 ]]; then
            return 1
          fi
          sleep "$$((attempt * 5))"
        done

        for architecture in 32 64; do
          steamclient="$$HOME/steamcmd/linux$$architecture/steamclient.so"
          if [[ -f "$$steamclient" ]]; then
            mkdir -p ".steam/sdk$$architecture"
            ln -sfn "$$steamclient" ".steam/sdk$$architecture/steamclient.so"
          fi
        done
        cd serverfiles
      }

      nex_steamcmd_update 1424230 linux
      [[ -f serverconfig_nex.txt ]] || cp serverconfig_default.txt serverconfig_nex.txt
      [[ "$$ADMIN_PASSWORD" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{12,}$$ ]] || {
        echo "Use at least 12 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore or hyphen for the Holdfast administrator password." >&2
        exit 1
      }
      tmp_config=$$(mktemp ./serverconfig_nex.XXXXXX)
      awk '$$1 !~ /^(server_admin_password|server_port|steam_query_port|steam_communications_port)$$/' serverconfig_nex.txt > "$$tmp_config"
      {
        printf 'server_admin_password %s\n' "$$ADMIN_PASSWORD"
        printf 'server_port 20100\nsteam_query_port 27000\nsteam_communications_port 8700\n'
        cat "$$tmp_config"
      } > "$$tmp_config.updated"
      mv "$$tmp_config.updated" serverconfig_nex.txt
      rm -f "$$tmp_config"
      mkdir -p logs_output logs_archive
      exec "./Holdfast NaW" -startserver -batchmode -nographics --serverheadless \
        -serverConfigFilePath serverconfig_nex.txt -logFile logs_output/server.log \
        -logArchivesDirectory logs_archive/ -p 20100
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

x-nex:
  name: IPFS Kubo
  summary: Run a persistent IPFS peer and HTTP retrieval gateway
  description: Use the published HTTP port to retrieve IPFS content. For inbound peers, use a dedicated
    Primary network and allow TCP and UDP port 4001 to the app address. The administrative RPC listener
    stays on container loopback.
  category: networking
  website: https://ipfs.tech/
  source: https://github.com/ipfs/kubo
  docs: https://docs.ipfs.tech/install/run-ipfs-inside-docker/
  scalable: false
  primary_service: ipfs-kubo
  architectures:
  - amd64
  - arm64
  web:
    service: ipfs-kubo
    scheme: http
    port: 8080
  options:
    PORT:
      label: Web port
      help: Host-published HTTP port when publishing is enabled. With a dedicated Primary network, use
        the application address on port 8080.
    DATA:
      label: IPFS repository
      help: Select This host. Holds the content-addressed data, peer identity and daemon configuration.
        Include this folder in a stopped Nex backup.
services:
  ipfs-kubo:
    image: ipfs/kubo:latest
    environment:
      IPFS_PROFILE: server
    ports:
    - ${PORT:-8170}:8080/tcp
    expose:
    - 4001/tcp
    - 4001/udp
    volumes:
    - ${DATA}:/data/ipfs
    entrypoint:
    - /sbin/tini
    - --
    - /bin/sh
    - -ec
    - |-
      run_ipfs() {
        if [ "$$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
          gosu ipfs ipfs "$$@"
        else
          ipfs "$$@"
        fi
      }
      if [ "$$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
        gosu ipfs test -w "$$IPFS_PATH" || chown -R ipfs:users "$$IPFS_PATH"
      fi
      if [ ! -f "$$IPFS_PATH/config" ]; then
        run_ipfs init --profile=server
      fi
      run_ipfs config Addresses.API /ip4/127.0.0.1/tcp/5001
      run_ipfs config Addresses.Gateway /ip4/0.0.0.0/tcp/8080
      exec /usr/local/bin/start_ipfs daemon --migrate=true --agent-version-suffix=docker
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

x-nex:
  name: Kerbal Space Program DarkMultiPlayer
  version: 0.3.8.5
  summary: Share a Kerbal Space Program universe with DarkMultiPlayer
  description: >-
    Keep the universe on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Install DarkMultiPlayer 0.3.8.5 on every Kerbal Space Program client and connect to the app’s
    Primary address on port 6702. Edit Config/Settings.txt in the managed folder to configure the
    game mode and allowlist. Make a stopped backup before applying updates.
  category: games
  website: https://d-mp.org/
  source: https://github.com/godarklight/DarkMultiPlayer
  docs: https://github.com/godarklight/DarkMultiPlayer#server
  license: MIT
  architectures: [amd64]
  tags: [multiplayer, space]
  options:
    DATA:
      label: Universe and server settings
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  kerbal-space-program-dmp:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/yolks:mono_latest
    working_dir: /data
    user: '0:0'
    entrypoint: [/bin/sh, -ec]
    command:
      - |
        umask 027
        chown container:container /data
        if [ ! -f .dmp-installed-0.3.8.5 ] || [ ! -s DMPServer.exe ]; then
          stage=$$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$$stage"' EXIT
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$$stage/server.zip" https://d-mp.org/builds/release/v0.3.8.5/DMPServer.zip
          printf '%s  %s\n' 'c1dbc89502fbd7837b80f6c1d5d5c08b87cc8c4063756f97b3f70d9b9177f28b' "$$stage/server.zip" | sha256sum -c -
          unzip -q "$$stage/server.zip" -d "$$stage"
          install -o container -g container -m 0644 "$$stage"/DMPServer/* /data/
          touch .dmp-installed-0.3.8.5
          rm -rf "$$stage"
          trap - EXIT
        fi
        exec setpriv --reuid=container --regid=container --init-groups mono DMPServer.exe
    expose:
      - 6702/tcp
      - 6702/udp
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/data
    stop_signal: SIGINT
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

    Start with one copy to bootstrap the administrator, then increase Copies on the
    Docker network. Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy. If the proxy is on the shared

  tags: [identity, single-sign-on, oidc, saml]
  options:
    PUBLIC_URL:
      label: Public HTTPS URL
      help: Full canonical HTTPS URL used by browsers and clients, for example https://identity.example.com. Configure the reverse proxy to overwrite X-Forwarded headers.
    TRUSTED_PROXIES:
      label: Trusted reverse proxy addresses
      help: Comma-separated addresses or CIDR ranges for the reverse proxies as seen by Keycloak. Keep the list limited to the networks your proxies use to reach Keycloak.
    CACHE_BIND_ADDRESS:
      label: Cluster bind address selection
      help: SITE_LOCAL selects a private container address. If the default binds to a network peers cannot reach, select a private overlay explicitly with match-address and a regular expression matching its subnet. Keycloak peers use TCP ports 7800 and 57800 on the overlay.
    DATABASE_URL:
      label: PostgreSQL JDBC URL
      help: Use a dedicated database reachable from all selected hosts, for example jdbc:postgresql://postgres.example.com:5432/keycloak. Include TLS options as required by your database.
    DATABASE_USER:
      label: PostgreSQL user
      help: Database role with permission to create and migrate the Keycloak schema.
    DATABASE_PASSWORD:
      label: PostgreSQL password
      type: password
    ADMIN_USER:
      label: Initial administrator
      help: Used to create the temporary administrator on first startup. Sign in, create a permanent administrator, then remove the temporary account.
    ADMIN_PASSWORD:
      label: Initial administrator password
      type: password
      help: Generate a strong temporary password. Changing this field after bootstrap does not reset an account.

      label: HTTP backend port
      help: When host publishing is enabled, keep this port private and use an HTTPS reverse proxy for client access. A proxy on the shared application network uses internal port 8080.
services:

    command: [start, --server-async-bootstrap=false]
    environment:
      KC_HTTP_ENABLED: "true"
      KC_HOSTNAME: "${PUBLIC_URL}"
      KC_PROXY_HEADERS: xforwarded
      KC_PROXY_TRUSTED_ADDRESSES: "${TRUSTED_PROXIES}"
      KC_DB: postgres
      KC_DB_URL: "${DATABASE_URL}"
      KC_DB_USERNAME: "${DATABASE_USER}"
      KC_DB_PASSWORD: "${DATABASE_PASSWORD}"
      KC_CACHE_STACK: jdbc-ping
      KC_CACHE_EMBEDDED_NETWORK_BIND_ADDRESS: "${CACHE_BIND_ADDRESS:-SITE_LOCAL}"
      KC_HEALTH_ENABLED: "true"
      KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME: "${ADMIN_USER:-admin}"
      KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD: "${ADMIN_PASSWORD}"
    ports:
      - "${PORT:-8091}:8080/tcp"
    healthcheck:
      test:
        - CMD
        - /bin/bash
        - -ec
        - >-
          exec 3<>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/9000;
          printf 'GET /health/ready HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n' >&3;
          read -r status <&3;
          [[ "$$status" == "HTTP/1.1 200 "* ]]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 4
      start_period: 5m
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: KissMP
  summary: Host a BeamNG.drive multiplayer world for KissMP
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Use the KissMP client mod version 0.8.0 and direct connect to the app’s Primary address on UDP
    3698. The first start installs the official server and creates config.json in the managed folder.
    Default settings disable public listing and UPnP.
  category: games
  website: https://github.com/TheHellBox/KISS-multiplayer
  source: https://github.com/TheHellBox/KISS-multiplayer
  docs: https://github.com/TheHellBox/KISS-multiplayer
  license: MIT server mod
  architectures:
  - amd64
  tags:
  - driving
  - multiplayer
  options:
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  kissmp:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/yolks:debian
    expose:
    - 3698/udp
    volumes:
    - ${DATA}:/home/container
    user: 1000:1000
    command:
    - /bin/bash
    - -ec
    - |
      download() {
        local url="$$1" sha256="$$2" target="$$3"
        curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 "$$url" -o "$$target"
        printf '%s  %s\n' "$$sha256" "$$target" | sha256sum --check --status || {
          echo "The server download did not match the release checksum." >&2
          return 1
        }
      }


      cd "$$HOME"
      if [ ! -x ./kissmp-server ]; then
        staging=$$(mktemp -d ./.kissmp-install.XXXXXX)
        trap 'rm -rf "$$staging"' EXIT
        download https://github.com/TheHellBox/KISS-multiplayer/releases/download/v0.8.0/KissMP_v0.8.0.zip \
          b0de0d10608e892e2a10faf8fba53177c9dd5a46a2ade5025848bfd59be1a05d "$$staging/release.zip"
        unzip -p "$$staging/release.zip" linux/kissmp-server > "$$staging/kissmp-server"
        chmod 755 "$$staging/kissmp-server"
        mv "$$staging/kissmp-server" ./kissmp-server
        rm -rf "$$staging"
        trap - EXIT
      fi
      exec ./kissmp-server
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

x-nex:
  name: LittleLink
  summary: Publish a profile page with links and social buttons
  description: The first start downloads and verifies the upstream v3.11.0 starter site. The app keeps your
    site edits in a managed folder and serves them with NGINX.
  category: development
  website: https://littlelink.io/
  source: https://github.com/sethcottle/littlelink
  docs: https://github.com/sethcottle/littlelink/releases/tag/v3.11.0
  license: MIT
  primary_service: littlelink
  architectures:
  - amd64
  - arm64
  post_install: Open the example page, then edit site/index.html and its assets in Site files. Back up this
    folder. Use an HTTPS proxy for public access.
  web:
    port: 80
  options:
    SITE:
      label: Site files
      help: Writable folder for the published site. An existing site/index.html is preserved on restart.
    PORT:
      label: Published HTTP port
      help: Internal HTTP port 80. This setting is used when host port publishing is enabled.
  version: 3.11.0
services:
  littlelink:
    image: docker.io/library/nginx:latest
    ports:
    - ${PORT:-18125}:80/tcp
    volumes:
    - ${SITE}:/nex-site
    entrypoint:
    - /bin/sh
    - -ec
    command:
    - |-
      if [ ! -s /nex-site/site/index.html ]; then
        stage=$$(mktemp -d /nex-site/.littlelink.XXXXXX)
        trap 'rm -rf "$$stage"' EXIT
        curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' --retry 2 --max-time 60 --max-filesize 4194304     https://codeload.github.com/sethcottle/littlelink/tar.gz/refs/tags/v3.11.0 -o "$$stage/upstream.tgz"
        (
          cd "$$stage"
          printf '%s\n' 'd88756f8e43240ede66041edff39ef268c8a47118b4297ee08363c9421201b91  upstream.tgz' | sha256sum -c -
        )
        mkdir "$$stage/site"
        tar -xzf "$$stage/upstream.tgz" -C "$$stage/site" --strip-components=1     littlelink-3.11.0/index.html littlelink-3.11.0/privacy.html littlelink-3.11.0/LICENSE.md     littlelink-3.11.0/css littlelink-3.11.0/fonts littlelink-3.11.0/images
        chmod 755 "$$stage/site"
        if ! mv -T "$$stage/site" /nex-site/site; then
          test -s /nex-site/site/index.html
        fi
        rm -rf "$$stage"
        trap - EXIT
      fi
      sed -i 's|/usr/share/nginx/html|/nex-site/site|g' /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
      exec /docker-entrypoint.sh nginx -g 'daemon off;'
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: Luanti
  summary: Host a private Minetest Game world with the Luanti engine
  description: >-
    Choose one host and a registered client-reachable primary network. On first start the server
    installs Minetest Game from the Luanti project and generates a world. In the Luanti client,
    choose Join Game and enter APP-IP, port 30000, a player name and the initial join password.
    Claim the administrator name before sharing the password. Take a stopped Nex backup before
    redeploying the image.
  category: games
  website: https://www.luanti.org/
  source: https://github.com/luanti-org/luanti
  docs: https://docs.luanti.org/for-server-hosts/setup/containers/
  license: LGPL-2.1-or-later
  architectures: [amd64, arm64]
  tags: [sandbox, building, co-op, dedicated-server]
  options:
    SERVER_NAME:
      label: Server name
      help: Use a single line of text for the server name.
    ADMIN_NAME:
      label: Administrator name
      help: Choose a Luanti player name and join under it before inviting other players.
    JOIN_PASSWORD:
      label: Initial join password
      type: password
      help: New players use this password once to create their local accounts. Use a single line of text.
    WORLD_DATA:
      label: World and settings
      help: Select This host. This folder includes the world, player accounts, mods and installed game.
services:
  luanti:
    image: ghcr.io/luanti-org/luanti:latest
    environment:
      SERVER_NAME: ${SERVER_NAME:-Nex Luanti}
      ADMIN_NAME: ${ADMIN_NAME}
      JOIN_PASSWORD: ${JOIN_PASSWORD}
    entrypoint: ['/bin/sh', '-ec']
    command:
      - |
        games=/var/lib/minetest/.minetest/games
        game="$$games/minetest"
        if [ ! -f "$$game/game.conf" ]; then
          if [ -e "$$game" ]; then
            echo "The Minetest Game folder is incomplete. Restore its game.conf or remove the incomplete folder." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          mkdir -p "$$games"
          temp=$$(mktemp -d /var/lib/minetest/.minetest/.nex-game.XXXXXX)
          trap 'rm -rf "$$temp"' EXIT
          curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \
            https://codeload.github.com/luanti-org/minetest_game/tar.gz/9e895af6e9feb98332fa1a778001442f5669bc20 \
            --output "$$temp/game.tar.gz"
          (cd "$$temp" && echo '325854277f8f171ebf395ac60aa8cd07250dd5a009f39f2027a56fa691e7e4ea  game.tar.gz' | sha256sum -c)
          mkdir "$$temp/minetest"
          tar -xzf "$$temp/game.tar.gz" -C "$$temp/minetest" --strip-components=1
          test -f "$$temp/minetest/game.conf"
          mv "$$temp/minetest" "$$game"
          rm -rf "$$temp"
          trap - EXIT
        fi
        umask 077
        printf '%s\n' "server_name = $$SERVER_NAME" "name = $$ADMIN_NAME" "default_password = $$JOIN_PASSWORD" \
          'disallow_empty_password = true' 'server_announce = false' 'enable_damage = true' \
          > /var/lib/minetest/nex.conf
        exec /usr/local/bin/luantiserver --config /var/lib/minetest/nex.conf --gameid minetest --worldname world
    expose: ['30000/udp']
    volumes:
      - ${WORLD_DATA}:/var/lib/minetest
    stop_grace_period: 1m
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: Midnight Ghost Hunt
  summary: Host online hide-and-seek matches
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Open UDP 7777 for game traffic, UDP 27015 for queries and UDP 7787 for the game beacon. Select
    the server in the in-game browser and enter the join password. SteamCMD downloads the server on
    first boot and checks for updates on restart. Allow time for the first download. Make a stopped
    backup before applying game updates.
  category: games
  website: https://store.steampowered.com/app/915810/
  source: https://github.com/nexvirtualization/nex-catalogue/tree/main/apps/midnight-ghost-hunt
  license: Proprietary game server
  architectures:
    - amd64
  tags:
    - steam
    - multiplayer
  options:
    JOIN_PASSWORD:
      label: Join password
      type: password
      help: Choose a password and share it with your players.
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  midnight-ghost-hunt:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/steamcmd:proton
    environment:
      JOIN_PASSWORD: ${JOIN_PASSWORD}
    expose:
      - 7777/udp
      - 27015/udp
      - 7787/udp
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/home/container
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    command:
      - /bin/bash
      - -ec
      - |
        # SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
        # Embedded in catalogue manifests that install a server through SteamCMD.
        # A package passes a dedicated-server app ID and either linux or windows.
        nex_steamcmd_update() {
          local app_id="$$1" platform="$$2"
          local archive attempt architecture steamclient
          local -a update=(+@ShutdownOnFailedCommand 1 +@NoPromptForPassword 1)

          cd "$$HOME"
          mkdir -p steamcmd serverfiles
          if [[ ! -x steamcmd/steamcmd.sh ]]; then
            archive=$$(mktemp)
            if ! curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \
              https://media.steampowered.com/client/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz -o "$$archive" \
              || ! tar -xzf "$$archive" -C steamcmd; then
              rm -f "$$archive"
              return 1
            fi
            rm -f "$$archive"
          fi

          if [[ "$$platform" == windows ]]; then
            update+=(+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows)
          fi
          update+=(+force_install_dir "$$HOME/serverfiles" +login anonymous +app_update "$$app_id" +quit)

          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh "$${update[@]}"; then
              break
            fi
            if [[ "$$attempt" == 3 ]]; then
              return 1
            fi
            sleep "$$((attempt * 5))"
          done

          for architecture in 32 64; do
            steamclient="$$HOME/steamcmd/linux$$architecture/steamclient.so"
            if [[ -f "$$steamclient" ]]; then
              mkdir -p ".steam/sdk$$architecture"
              ln -sfn "$$steamclient" ".steam/sdk$$architecture/steamclient.so"
            fi
          done
          cd serverfiles
        }

        nex_steamcmd_update 1118810 windows
        export STEAM_COMPAT_CLIENT_INSTALL_PATH="$$HOME/.steam/steam"
        export STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH="$$HOME/.proton"
        mkdir -p "$$STEAM_COMPAT_CLIENT_INSTALL_PATH" "$$STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH"
        exec xvfb-run -a proton run MidnightGhostHunt/Binaries/Win64/MidnightGhostHuntServer-Win64-Shipping.exe -server -log -port=7777 -queryport=27015 -BeaconPort=7787 -multihome=0.0.0.0 -Map=Asylum '-Gamename=Nex Midnight Ghost Hunt' '-Gamemode=4v4 Hunt' -BotDifficulty=Auto "-password=$$JOIN_PASSWORD"

      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.

    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    command:
      - /bin/bash
      - -ec
      - |
        cd "$$HOME"
        file=server-release.jar
        pending=$$(mktemp)
        trap 'rm -f "$$pending"' EXIT
        if curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 --remote-time      --time-cond "$$file" 'https://github.com/Anuken/Mindustry/releases/latest/download/server-release.jar' -o "$$pending"; then
          if [[ -s "$$pending" ]]; then
            mv "$$pending" "$$file"
          fi
        elif [[ ! -s "$$file" ]]; then
          exit 1
        else
          printf 'Update unavailable, using the last installed Mindustry server.\n' >&2
        fi
        test -s "$$file"
        rm -f "$$pending"
        trap - EXIT
        exec java -jar "$$file" host

    Edition client. Manage the world and Lua plugins from the data folder. Make a stopped backup

  docs: https://book.cuberite.org/
  license: Apache-2.0
  architectures: [amd64]

    DATA:
      label: World, extensions and settings
      help: >-
        Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  minecraft-cuberite:
    image: ghcr.io/itzg/minecraft-server:latest
    working_dir: /data
    entrypoint: [/bin/bash, -ec]
    command:
      - |
        chown 1000:1000 /data
        if [ ! -f /data/.cuberite-installed ]; then
          set -o pipefail
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 'https://download.cuberite.org/linux-x86_64/Cuberite.tar.gz' | gosu 1000:1000 tar -xz --no-same-owner -C /data

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: Minecraft NanoLimbo
  summary: Hold Java Edition players while a backend is unavailable
  description: >-
    Keep the server folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can
    reach. Install NanoLimbo as a fallback backend for your Minecraft proxy. Use its Primary address
    on TCP 25565 in the proxy and configure forwarding in settings.yml. Restrict direct access to
    the proxy.
  category: games
  website: https://github.com/Nan1t/NanoLimbo
  source: https://github.com/Nan1t/NanoLimbo
  docs: https://github.com/Nan1t/NanoLimbo#player-info-forwarding
  license: GPL-3.0
  architectures: [amd64, arm64]
  tags: [minecraft, proxy]
  options:
    DATA:
      label: World, extensions and settings
      help: >-
        Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  minecraft-nanolimbo:
    image: ghcr.io/itzg/minecraft-server:java21
    working_dir: /data
    entrypoint: [/bin/sh, -ec]
    command:
      - |
        chown 1000:1000 /data
        if [ ! -s /data/NanoLimbo.jar ]; then
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o /data/.server.jar.new 'https://github.com/Nan1t/NanoLimbo/releases/download/v1.13.0/NanoLimbo.jar'
          chown 1000:1000 /data/.server.jar.new
          mv /data/.server.jar.new /data/NanoLimbo.jar
        fi

        if [ ! -f /data/settings.yml ]; then
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o /data/.settings.yml.new 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nan1t/NanoLimbo/v1.13.0/src/main/resources/settings.yml'
          sed -i -e 's/^  ip: "localhost"$$/  ip: "0.0.0.0"/' -e 's/^  port: 65535$$/  port: 25565/' /data/.settings.yml.new
          chown 1000:1000 /data/.settings.yml.new
          mv /data/.settings.yml.new /data/settings.yml
        fi

        exec gosu 1000:1000 java -Xmx512M -jar /data/NanoLimbo.jar
    healthcheck:
      disable: true
    expose:
      - 25565/tcp
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/data
    stop_grace_period: 60s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

x-nex:
  name: Minecraft VIAaaS
  summary: Bridge Java Edition client and server protocol versions
  description: >-
    Keep the server folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can
    reach. Point wildcard DNS at the Primary address and set the matching hostname and permitted
    backends in the VIAaaS configuration. The proxy listens on TCP 25565 and its setup web interface
    uses HTTPS on TCP 25543.
  category: games
  website: https://viaversion.com/
  source: https://github.com/ViaVersion/VIAaaS
  docs: https://github.com/ViaVersion/VIAaaS/blob/master/INSTALL.md
  license: AGPL-3.0
  architectures: [amd64, arm64]
  tags: [minecraft, proxy]
  options:
    DATA:
      label: World, extensions and settings
      help: >-
        Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  minecraft-viaaas:
    image: ghcr.io/itzg/minecraft-server:java21
    working_dir: /data
    entrypoint: [/bin/sh, -ec]
    command:
      - |
        chown 1000:1000 /data
        if [ ! -s /data/VIAaaS.jar ]; then
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o /data/.server.jar.new 'https://github.com/ViaVersion/VIAaaS/releases/download/v0.5.2/VIAaaS-0.5.2%2B022e465-all.jar'
          chown 1000:1000 /data/.server.jar.new
          mv /data/.server.jar.new /data/VIAaaS.jar
        fi

        exec gosu 1000:1000 java -Xmx1G -jar /data/VIAaaS.jar -sslPort=25543
    healthcheck:
      disable: true
    expose:
      - 25565/tcp
      - 25543/tcp
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/data
    stop_grace_period: 60s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

  name: NGINX
  summary: Run a stateless web server and verify Swarm routing
  description: >-
    NGINX serves a plain-text status page that includes the responding container hostname.
    Use it to check that one published HTTP port reaches several copies and stays available
    during replica replacement. This starter runs without persistent folders.
  category: networking
  website: https://nginx.org/
  source: https://github.com/nginx/nginx
  docs: https://docs.docker.com/engine/swarm/ingress/
  license: BSD-2-Clause
  scalable: true
  scale: [nginx]
  primary_service: nginx
  web: {port: 80}
  tags: [web-server, docker, swarm]
  post_install: >-
    In Basics, set Copies to two or more. Keep the default Docker network and enable host
    publishing. Send several fresh HTTP requests to the same published endpoint and compare
    the replica names in the response body or X-Nex-Replica header.
  options:
    PORT:
      label: Web port
      help: Published HTTP port for the Swarm ingress endpoint. NGINX listens on container port 80.
services:
  nginx:
    image: docker.io/library/nginx:latest
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -ec
      - |
        cat > /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf <<'NGINX'
        server {
          listen 80 default_server;
          listen [::]:80 default_server;
          default_type text/plain;

          location = /healthz {
            return 200 "ok\n";
          }

          location / {
            add_header Cache-Control "no-store";
            add_header X-Nex-Replica $$hostname;
            return 200 "NGINX replica: $$hostname\n";
          }
        }
        NGINX
        exec nginx -g 'daemon off;'
    ports:
      - "${PORT:-8088}:80/tcp"
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

    command:

        if [[ ! "$$JOIN_PASSWORD" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_@.+-]+$$ ]]; then
          echo "Use letters, digits, or _ @ . + - in the join password." >&2
          exit 1
        fi

        if [[ ! "$$ADMIN_PASSWORD" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_@.+-]+$$ ]]; then
          echo "Use letters, digits, or _ @ . + - in the administrator password." >&2
          exit 1
        fi

        # SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
        # Embedded in catalogue manifests that install a server through SteamCMD.
        # A package passes a dedicated-server app ID and either linux or windows.
        nex_steamcmd_update() {
          local app_id="$$1" platform="$$2"
          local archive attempt architecture steamclient
          local -a update=(+@ShutdownOnFailedCommand 1 +@NoPromptForPassword 1)

          cd "$$HOME"
          mkdir -p steamcmd serverfiles
          if [[ ! -x steamcmd/steamcmd.sh ]]; then
            archive=$$(mktemp)
            if ! curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \
              https://media.steampowered.com/client/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz -o "$$archive" \
              || ! tar -xzf "$$archive" -C steamcmd; then

              return 1

          fi
          update+=(+force_install_dir "$$HOME/serverfiles" +login anonymous +app_update "$$app_id" +quit)

            if ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh "$${update[@]}"; then
              break
            fi
            if [[ "$$attempt" == 3 ]]; then
              return 1
            fi
            sleep "$$((attempt * 5))"
          done

          for architecture in 32 64; do
            steamclient="$$HOME/steamcmd/linux$$architecture/steamclient.so"
            if [[ -f "$$steamclient" ]]; then
              mkdir -p ".steam/sdk$$architecture"
              ln -sfn "$$steamclient" ".steam/sdk$$architecture/steamclient.so"

          [[ ! -f "$$stamp" ]] || exit 0
          stage=$$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$$stage"' EXIT
          curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 "$$url" -o "$$stage/runtime.exe"
          timeout 10m xvfb-run -a -s "-nolisten tcp" proton run "$$stage/runtime.exe" /install /quiet /norestart || status=$$?
          # Windows exit code 3010 (restart requested) is truncated to 194 on Linux.

        exec xvfb-run -a -s "-nolisten tcp" proton run "$$server" '?listen' \

    stop_signal: SIGINT

  scalable: false
  primary_service: ntfy
  tags: [notifications, push, alerts]
  options:
    BASE_URL:
      label: Public web address
      help: Required full client-facing URL, including scheme and any port, for example https://notify.example.com. Needed to build notification attachment links.
    ADMIN_USER:
      label: Initial administrator
      help: Administrator managed by Nex settings. Use letters, digits, underscores or hyphens. Changing this name removes the previous provisioned account at restart.
    ADMIN_PASSWORD:
      label: Initial administrator password
      type: password
      help: Choose a strong password or use Nex Generate. Nex hashes it inside the container; saving a changed password and restarting updates this administrator.
    PORT:
      label: Web port
      help: Host-published HTTP port; with a dedicated Primary network and host publishing off, connect to the app address on port 80. A reverse proxy must support long-lived streaming requests. Set Public web address to the client-facing URL.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: Nuclear Option
  summary: Host multiplayer flight combat missions
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Use the online server browser or the app’s Primary address on UDP 27015. UDP 7777 is the default
    query port. Edit the generated DedicatedServerConfig.json in the managed serverfiles folder to
    set the mission and password. SteamCMD downloads the server on first boot and checks for updates
    on restart. Allow time for the first download. Make a stopped backup before applying game updates.
  category: games
  website: https://store.steampowered.com/app/2168680/
  source: https://github.com/nexvirtualization/nex-catalogue/tree/main/apps/nuclear-option
  docs: https://github.com/Shockfront-Studios/Nuclear-Option-Server-Tools
  license: Proprietary game server
  architectures:
    - amd64
  tags:
    - steam
    - multiplayer
  options:
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  nuclear-option:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/steamcmd:debian
    expose:
      - 27015/udp
      - 7777/udp
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/home/container
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    command:
      - /bin/bash
      - -ec
      - |
        # SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
        # Embedded in catalogue manifests that install a server through SteamCMD.
        # A package passes a dedicated-server app ID and either linux or windows.
        nex_steamcmd_update() {
          local app_id="$$1" platform="$$2"
          local archive attempt architecture steamclient
          local -a update=(+@ShutdownOnFailedCommand 1 +@NoPromptForPassword 1)

          cd "$$HOME"
          mkdir -p steamcmd serverfiles
          if [[ ! -x steamcmd/steamcmd.sh ]]; then
            archive=$$(mktemp)
            if ! curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \
              https://media.steampowered.com/client/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz -o "$$archive" \
              || ! tar -xzf "$$archive" -C steamcmd; then
              rm -f "$$archive"
              return 1
            fi
            rm -f "$$archive"
          fi

          if [[ "$$platform" == windows ]]; then
            update+=(+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows)
          fi
          update+=(+force_install_dir "$$HOME/serverfiles" +login anonymous +app_update "$$app_id" +quit)

          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh "$${update[@]}"; then
              break
            fi
            if [[ "$$attempt" == 3 ]]; then
              return 1
            fi
            sleep "$$((attempt * 5))"
          done

          for architecture in 32 64; do
            steamclient="$$HOME/steamcmd/linux$$architecture/steamclient.so"
            if [[ -f "$$steamclient" ]]; then
              mkdir -p ".steam/sdk$$architecture"
              ln -sfn "$$steamclient" ".steam/sdk$$architecture/steamclient.so"
            fi
          done
          cd serverfiles
        }

        nex_steamcmd_update 3930080 linux
        export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$$PWD/linux64$${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:$$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"
        exec ./NuclearOptionServer.x86_64

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: Onset
  summary: Run multiplayer scenarios for the Onset scripting sandbox
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Use UDP 7777 for gameplay, UDP 7776 for discovery and TCP 7775 for client file downloads. Place
    gamemode assets in the managed server folder before enabling them. SteamCMD downloads the server
    on first boot and checks for updates on restart. Allow time for the first download. Make a stopped
    backup before applying game updates.
  category: games
  website: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1105810/
  source: https://github.com/nexvirtualization/nex-catalogue/tree/main/apps/onset
  docs: https://dev.playonset.com/wiki/DedicatedServer
  license: Proprietary game server
  architectures:
    - amd64
  tags:
    - steam
    - multiplayer
  options:
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  onset:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/steamcmd:debian
    expose:
      - 7777/udp
      - 7776/udp
      - 7775/tcp
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/home/container
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    command:
      - /bin/bash
      - -ec
      - |
        # SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
        # Embedded in catalogue manifests that install a server through SteamCMD.
        # A package passes a dedicated-server app ID and either linux or windows.
        nex_steamcmd_update() {
          local app_id="$$1" platform="$$2"
          local archive attempt architecture steamclient
          local -a update=(+@ShutdownOnFailedCommand 1 +@NoPromptForPassword 1)

          cd "$$HOME"
          mkdir -p steamcmd serverfiles
          if [[ ! -x steamcmd/steamcmd.sh ]]; then
            archive=$$(mktemp)
            if ! curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \
              https://media.steampowered.com/client/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz -o "$$archive" \
              || ! tar -xzf "$$archive" -C steamcmd; then
              rm -f "$$archive"
              return 1
            fi
            rm -f "$$archive"
          fi

          if [[ "$$platform" == windows ]]; then
            update+=(+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows)
          fi
          update+=(+force_install_dir "$$HOME/serverfiles" +login anonymous +app_update "$$app_id" +quit)

          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh "$${update[@]}"; then
              break
            fi
            if [[ "$$attempt" == 3 ]]; then
              return 1
            fi
            sleep "$$((attempt * 5))"
          done

          for architecture in 32 64; do
            steamclient="$$HOME/steamcmd/linux$$architecture/steamclient.so"
            if [[ -f "$$steamclient" ]]; then
              mkdir -p ".steam/sdk$$architecture"
              ln -sfn "$$steamclient" ".steam/sdk$$architecture/steamclient.so"
            fi
          done
          cd serverfiles
        }

        nex_steamcmd_update 1204170 linux
        exec ./OnsetServer --noinput
