x-nex:
  name: open.mp
  summary: Host a San Andreas multiplayer game mode
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Use the open.mp launcher to join the app’s Primary address on UDP 7777. The first start installs
    the official Linux server with the bundled GunGame mode. Stop the app to edit server/config.json
    or replace the game mode. Remote console access is disabled in the initial settings.
  category: games
  website: https://open.mp/
  source: https://github.com/openmultiplayer/open.mp
  docs: https://open.mp/docs/server/Installation
  license: MPL-2.0 game server
  architectures:
  - amd64
  tags:
  - sandbox
  - multiplayer
  options:
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  openmp:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/games:samp
    expose:
    - 7777/udp
    volumes:
    - ${DATA}:/home/container
    user: 1000:1000
    command:
    - /bin/bash
    - -ec
    - |
      download() {
        local url="$$1" sha256="$$2" target="$$3"
        curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 "$$url" -o "$$target"
        printf '%s  %s\n' "$$sha256" "$$target" | sha256sum --check --status || {
          echo "The server download did not match the release checksum." >&2
          return 1
        }
      }


      cd "$$HOME"
      if [ ! -x ./server/omp-server ]; then
        staging=$$(mktemp -d ./.openmp-install.XXXXXX)
        trap 'rm -rf "$$staging"' EXIT
        download https://github.com/openmultiplayer/open.mp/releases/download/v1.6.7.3218/open.mp-linux-x86.tar.gz \
          0f7bfe70bb68ea780fe24a910b69412046e53d10feb65a9d4a9de8ff1f7f1329 "$$staging/release.tar.gz"
        tar -xzf "$$staging/release.tar.gz" -C "$$staging"
        chmod 755 "$$staging/Server/omp-server"
        printf '%s\n' '{"name":"Nex open.mp","announce":false,"network":{"port":7777},"pawn":{"main_scripts":["gungame 1"]},"rcon":{"enable":false}}' > "$$staging/Server/config.json"
        mv "$$staging/Server" ./server
        rm -rf "$$staging"
        trap - EXIT
      fi
      cd ./server
      exec ./omp-server
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

      label: Server data

    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    command:
      - /bin/bash
      - -ec
      - |
        cd "$$HOME"
        if [[ ! -x openra-20250330/AppRun ]]; then
          temporary=$$(mktemp -d "$$HOME/.openra-install.XXXXXX")
          trap 'rm -rf "$$temporary"' EXIT
          cd "$$temporary"
          curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 'https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/releases/download/release-20250330/OpenRA-Dune-2000-x86_64.AppImage' -o OpenRA.AppImage
          printf '%s  %s\n' '7585986bf0cd488debaec3fadf853c1901003eff945dbad5de95b0b6bd781a67' OpenRA.AppImage | sha256sum -c -
          chmod +x OpenRA.AppImage
          ./OpenRA.AppImage --appimage-extract >/dev/null
          test -x squashfs-root/AppRun
          cd "$$HOME"
          mv "$$temporary/squashfs-root" openra-20250330
          rm -rf "$$temporary"
          trap - EXIT
        fi
        exec ./openra-20250330/AppRun --server 'Server.Name=Nex Dune 2000' Server.ListenPort=1234 Server.AdvertiseOnline=False Server.ShareAnonymizedIPs=False "Server.Password=$$JOIN_PASSWORD"

x-nex:
  name: OpenRemote
  summary: Manage IoT devices, data, and automation rules
  description: Use the configured browser hostname and route HTTPS and MQTTS as needed. Set the external
    HTTPS port to match Keycloak’s public URL. Sign in as admin with the supplied password and back up the

  category: home-automation
  website: https://openremote.io
  source: https://github.com/openremote/core
  docs: https://github.com/openremote/core/blob/main/docker-compose.yml
  primary_service: openremote
  post_install: Use the configured browser hostname and route HTTPS and MQTTS as needed. Set the external
    HTTPS port to match Keycloak’s public URL. Sign in as admin with the supplied password and back up the
    database and manager data.
  architectures:
  - amd64
  - arm64
  web:
    port: 443
    scheme: https
  options:
    PUBLIC_HOST:
      label: Public host
      help: Enter the deployment value described in the upstream setup guide.
    ACME_EMAIL:
      label: Acme email
      help: Enter the deployment value described in the upstream setup guide.
    ADMIN_PASSWORD:
      label: Admin password
      help: Use the credential or secret required by the upstream configuration.
      type: password
    DB_PASSWORD:
      label: Db password
      help: Use the credential or secret required by the upstream configuration.
      type: password
    EXTERNAL_HTTPS_PORT:
      label: External https port
      help: Enter the deployment value described in the upstream setup guide.
    PORT:
      label: Published HTTP port
      help: Host-published HTTPS port. For a reverse proxy, forward to internal TCP port 443.
    HTTP_PORT:
      label: Published HTTP or ACME port
      help: Host-published port for the internal 80/tcp endpoint.
    MQTTS_PORT:
      label: Published MQTTS port
      help: Host-published port for the internal 8883/tcp endpoint.
    PROXY_DATA:
      label: TLS and proxy state
      help: Managed directory mounted at /deployment. Choose storage writable by the application.
    MANAGER_DATA:
      label: Manager data
      help: Managed writable directory mounted at /storage.
    DB_DATA:
      label: OpenRemote database
      help: Managed writable directory mounted at /var/lib/postgresql/data.
services:
  openremote:
    image: docker.io/openremote/proxy:latest
    ports:
    - ${PORT:-23548}:443/tcp
    - ${HTTP_PORT:-24548}:80/tcp
    - ${MQTTS_PORT:-25548}:8883/tcp
    volumes:
    - ${PROXY_DATA}:/deployment
    environment:
      DOMAINNAME: ${PUBLIC_HOST}
      LE_EMAIL: ${ACME_EMAIL:-}
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
  postgresql:
    image: docker.io/openremote/postgresql:latest-slim
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: openremote
      POSTGRES_USER: postgres
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
    - ${DB_DATA}:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
  keycloak:
    image: docker.io/openremote/keycloak:latest
    environment:
      KC_DB_URL_HOST: postgresql
      KC_DB_URL_DATABASE: openremote
      KC_DB_USERNAME: postgres
      KC_DB_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      KC_HOSTNAME: https://${PUBLIC_HOST}:${EXTERNAL_HTTPS_PORT:-443}/auth
      KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${ADMIN_PASSWORD}
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
  manager:
    image: docker.io/openremote/manager:latest
    environment:
      OR_DB_HOST: postgresql
      OR_DB_NAME: openremote
      OR_DB_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      OR_HOSTNAME: ${PUBLIC_HOST}
      OR_SSL_PORT: ${EXTERNAL_HTTPS_PORT:-443}
      OR_ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      OR_METRICS_ENABLED: 'false'
    volumes:
    - ${MANAGER_DATA}:/storage
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

  website: https://www.opensignlabs.com
  source: https://github.com/opensignlabs/opensign
  docs: https://github.com/opensignlabs/opensign/blob/main/docker-compose.yml
  primary_service: opensign
  post_install: Provision MongoDB, SMTP, and a document-signing certificate in PKCS#12 format. Use HTTPS,
    fill in the signing certificate and passphrase, and set up the initial account.
  license: AGPL-3.0
  architectures:
  - amd64
  - arm64
  web:
    port: 8081
  options:
    PUBLIC_URL:
      label: Public url
      help: Full browser-facing URL, including scheme and any nonstandard port.
    APP_ID:
      label: App id
      help: Enter the deployment value described in the upstream setup guide.
    MASTER_KEY:
      label: Master key
      help: Use the credential or secret required by the upstream configuration.
      type: password
    MONGO_URI:
      label: Mongo uri
      help: Use the credential or secret required by the upstream configuration.
      type: password
    SMTP_HOST:
      label: Smtp host
      help: Enter the deployment value described in the upstream setup guide.
    SMTP_PORT:
      label: Smtp port
      help: Enter the deployment value described in the upstream setup guide.
    SMTP_USER:
      label: Smtp user
      help: Enter the deployment value described in the upstream setup guide.
    SMTP_PASSWORD:
      label: Smtp password
      help: Use the credential or secret required by the upstream configuration.
      type: password
    SIGNING_CERT:
      label: Signing certificate
      help: Enter the base64-encoded PKCS#12 signing certificate.
      type: password
    CERT_PASSWORD:
      label: Cert password
      help: Use the credential or secret required by the upstream configuration.
      type: password
    PORT:
      label: Published HTTP port
      help: Host-published port. The app listens on TCP port 8081 inside Nex.
    DATA:
      label: Signed documents and files
      help: Managed directory mounted at /usr/src/app/files. Choose storage writable by the application.

    image: docker.io/library/caddy:latest
    ports:
    - ${PORT:-23539}:8081/tcp
    entrypoint:
    - /bin/sh
    command:
    - -ec
    - |-
      printf '%s\n' '{
        auto_https off
      }
      :8081 {
        handle_path /api/* {
          reverse_proxy server:8080
        }
        handle {
          reverse_proxy client:3000
        }

    deploy:
      replicas: 1

    image: docker.io/opensign/opensignserver:main

      APP_ID: ${APP_ID}
      MASTER_KEY: ${MASTER_KEY}
      MONGODB_URI: ${MONGO_URI}
      PARSE_MOUNT: /app
      SERVER_URL: ${PUBLIC_URL}/api/app

      SMTP_ENABLE: 'true'

      SMTP_PORT: ${SMTP_PORT:-587}
      SMTP_USER_EMAIL: ${SMTP_USER}

      replicas: 1

    environment:
      REACT_APP_SERVERURL: ${PUBLIC_URL}/api/app
      REACT_APP_APPID: ${APP_ID}
      PUBLIC_URL: ${PUBLIC_URL}

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: OpenTTD
  summary: Build competing or cooperative transport networks
  description: >-
    Run one copy on a selected host and keep saves on This host. In Network, choose a cluster
    VLAN or routed private network reachable by players. In the OpenTTD multiplayer menu, add
    the app's Primary address and port 3979. Allow TCP and UDP. Enter the join password and
    use a matching game version. Back up saves before updating.
  category: games
  website: https://www.openttd.org/
  source: https://github.com/bateau84/openttd
  docs: https://wiki.openttd.org/en/Manual/Dedicated%20server
  license: GPL-2.0-only
  architectures: [amd64]
  tags: [trains, simulation, multiplayer]
  options:
    SERVER_NAME:
      label: Server name
      help: Sets the initial server name. After installation, edit openttd.cfg in Files while the app is stopped.
    JOIN_PASSWORD:
      label: Join password
      type: password
      help: Use Generate and share the password with players. To rotate it, edit openttd.cfg while the app is stopped.
    DATA:
      label: Saves and settings
      help: Choose This host. Include this folder in a stopped backup. The server resumes the latest autosave.
services:
  openttd:
    image: docker.io/bateau/openttd:15.3
    environment:
      SERVER_NAME: ${SERVER_NAME:-Nex OpenTTD}
      JOIN_PASSWORD: ${JOIN_PASSWORD}
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -ec
      - |
        data=/home/openttd/.openttd
        config="$$data/openttd.cfg"
        if [ ! -f "$$config" ]; then
          umask 077
          printf '%s\n' '[network]' 'server_game_type = local' "server_name = $$SERVER_NAME" \
            "server_password = $$JOIN_PASSWORD" '[gui]' 'autosave_on_exit = true' > "$$config.tmp"
          mv "$$config.tmp" "$$config"
        fi
        export loadgame=false
        for save in "$$data"/save/autosave/*.sav; do
          if [ -f "$$save" ]; then
            export loadgame=last-autosave
            break
          fi
        done
        exec /openttd.sh
    expose:
      - "3979/tcp"
      - "3979/udp"
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/home/openttd/.openttd
    stop_grace_period: 60s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

x-nex:
  name: Path of Titans
  summary: Host a persistent Path of Titans community server
  description: >-
    Use an x86-64 host, choose This host for Server data, and select a registered primary
    network reachable by your players. Obtain a server hosting token through your Alderon
    Games account. First boot downloads the publisher’s server and creates a local database.
    The game uses UDP 7777 and community server queries use TCP 7778. Choose the server in
    the game’s Community Servers browser. A restart checks for updates. Make a stopped backup
    before applying game updates.
  category: games
  website: https://pathoftitans.com/
  source: https://github.com/Alderon-Games/pot-community-servers
  docs: https://hosting.pathoftitans.wiki/setup/server-setup
  license: Proprietary game server
  architectures: [amd64]
  tags: [survival, multiplayer]
  options:
    HOSTING_TOKEN:
      label: Alderon hosting token
      type: password
      help: Create a server hosting token in your Alderon Games account under Games.
    SERVER_NAME:
      label: Server name
      help: Name displayed in the Community Servers browser.
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Keep the installed server, configuration, local database and instance ID together.
services:
  path-of-titans:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/steamcmd:debian
    environment:
      HOSTING_TOKEN: ${HOSTING_TOKEN}
      SERVER_NAME: ${SERVER_NAME:-Nex Path of Titans}
    expose:
      - 7777/udp
      - 7778/tcp
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/home/container
    command:
      - /bin/bash
      - -ec
      - |
        set -o pipefail
        umask 077
        cd "$$HOME"
        if [[ ! -x AlderonGamesCmd ]]; then
          pending=$$(mktemp)
          trap 'rm -f "$$pending"' EXIT
          curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \
            https://launcher-cdn.alderongames.com/AlderonGamesCmd-Linux-x64 -o "$$pending"
          chmod 0700 "$$pending"
          mv "$$pending" AlderonGamesCmd
          trap - EXIT
        fi
        if [[ ! -s server-guid ]]; then
          cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid > server-guid
        fi
        redact_token() {
          local line
          while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$$line" ]]; do
            printf '%s\n' "$${line//"$$HOSTING_TOKEN"/[redacted]}"
          done
        }
        ./AlderonGamesCmd --game path-of-titans --server true --beta-branch production \
          --auth-token "$$HOSTING_TOKEN" --install-dir "$$HOME/server" 2>&1 | redact_token
        cd server
        exec ./PathOfTitansServer.sh 'Island?listen?MaxPlayers=50' -Port=7777 \
          -QueryPort=7778 -nullRHI "-ServerName=$$SERVER_NAME" \
          "-ServerGUID=$$(cat ../server-guid)" -BranchKey=production -Database=Local -log
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

x-nex:
  name: Peergos
  summary: Encrypted file storage, sharing, and collaboration on a peer-to-peer network.
  description: Configure a TLS reverse proxy for the public domain and the wildcard subdomains used
    by Peergos. Attach the app to a dedicated Primary network that accepts TCP and UDP 4001 for peers.
    Create an invitation with the documented quota token command before signing up.
  category: documents
  website: https://github.com/Peergos/Peergos
  source: https://github.com/Peergos/Peergos
  docs: https://github.com/Peergos/Peergos#usage---self-hosting-with-docker
  primary_service: peergos
  scalable: false
  license: AGPL-3.0
  web:
    port: 8000
  options:
    DOMAIN:
      label: Public domain
      help: Bare hostname for the HTTPS proxy, without a scheme or path.
    PUBLIC_IPV4:
      label: Public peer IPv4 address
      help: Public IPv4 address that forwards TCP and UDP 4001 to the app.
    DATA:
      label: Peergos data
      help: Keep peergos data in this managed folder between restarts.
    PORT:
      label: Web port
      help: Host-published TCP port. With a dedicated Primary network and host publishing off, use the
        application address on port 8000.
services:
  peergos:
    image: ghcr.io/peergos/web-ui:master
    expose:
    - 4001/tcp
    - 4001/udp
    command:
    - daemon
    - -listen-host
    - 0.0.0.0
    - -public-domain
    - ${DOMAIN}
    - -public-server
    - 'true'
    - -announce-ipfs-addresses
    - /ip4/${PUBLIC_IPV4}/tcp/4001,/ip4/${PUBLIC_IPV4}/udp/4001/quic-v1
    - -log-to-console
    - 'true'
    volumes:
    - ${DATA}:/opt/peergos/data
    ports:
    - ${PORT:-8000}:8000/tcp
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: Pi-hole
  summary: Block advertising domains across your home network
  description: DNS filtering for your LAN. In Install, Network choose Primary network, a registered cluster VLAN
    reachable by your clients, then Fixed with an unused address/prefix and Default gateway. Leave Also publish
    ports on host addresses unchecked. Open http://APP-IP/admin/ and sign in with the generated Administrator password.
    Set router/client DNS to APP-IP, port 53 over both TCP and UDP. The shared-network default alone cannot serve
    LAN DNS. DNS listens on all app interfaces; attach only trusted client networks. DHCP and NTP serving are disabled.
    On Basics choose Runs on, Only these hosts and one host; keep state folders on This host. This keeps one copy
    on that host with no automatic failover. Use ACTIONS, Back up now with the stopped-copy option and select all
    state folders before updates.
  category: networking
  website: https://pi-hole.net
  source: https://github.com/pi-hole/pi-hole
  license: EUPL-1.2
  scalable: false
  tags:
  - dns
  - ad-blocking
  - privacy
  options:
    TZ:
      label: Time zone
      help: IANA time zone for logs, such as Etc/UTC.
    PASSWORD:
      label: Administrator password
      help: Use Generate for a unique password for http://APP-IP/admin/. Password answers are held in deployment
        settings and backup manifests; protect Nex access and the backup repository.
      type: password
    PORT:
      label: Web port
      help: Only the optional host management endpoint. On Network choose a registered cluster VLAN reachable by
        your clients, Fixed address/prefix and Default gateway, and leave host publication off; use http://APP-IP/admin/
        and APP-IP:53 for DNS instead.
    CONFIG:
      label: Pi-hole configuration
      help: Keep Pi-hole configuration on This host. Nex creates its persistent /etc/pihole volume; no host directory
        bootstrap is needed. Include this folder in a stopped Nex backup to preserve passwords, blocklists, settings
        and databases.
services:
  pi-hole:
    image: pihole/pihole:latest
    environment:
      TZ: ${TZ:-Etc/UTC}
      FTLCONF_webserver_api_password: ${PASSWORD}
      FTLCONF_dns_listeningMode: ALL
      FTLCONF_dhcp_active: 'false'
      FTLCONF_ntp_ipv4_active: 'false'
      FTLCONF_ntp_ipv6_active: 'false'
    ports:
    - ${PORT:-8083}:80/tcp
    expose:
    - 53/tcp
    - 53/udp
    volumes:
    - ${CONFIG}:/etc/pihole
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: PixARK
  summary: Host a persistent voxel survival world
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Steam downloads the dedicated server on first boot. In the PixARK session browser, search for
    Nex PixARK or add the app’s Primary address and UDP 27016 to Steam favorites. Players need UDP
    27015 for the game and TCP 27018 to load the cube world. The world seed and save directory stay
    fixed to keep the same world across restarts. Make a stopped backup before applying game updates.
  category: games
  website: https://store.steampowered.com/app/593600/
  source: https://github.com/nexvirtualization/nex-catalogue/tree/main/apps/pixark
  docs: https://pixark.fandom.com/wiki/Server_configuration
  license: Proprietary game server
  architectures:
    - amd64
  tags:
    - survival
    - steam
  options:
    JOIN_PASSWORD:
      label: Join password
      type: password
      help: Use letters, digits, or _ @ . + -.
    ADMIN_PASSWORD:
      label: Administrator password
      type: password
      help: Use letters, digits, or _ @ . + -.
    DATA:
      label: Game files, compatibility prefix, and settings
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  pixark:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/steamcmd:proton
    environment:
      JOIN_PASSWORD: ${JOIN_PASSWORD}
      WINEDEBUG: -all
      PROTON_USE_XALIA: '0'
      ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${ADMIN_PASSWORD}
    expose:
      - 27015/udp
      - 27016/udp
      - 27018/tcp
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/home/container
    stop_grace_period: 120s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    command:
      - /bin/bash
      - -ec
      - |
        if [[ ! "$$JOIN_PASSWORD" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_@.+-]+$$ ]]; then
          echo "Use letters, digits, or _ @ . + - in the join password." >&2
          exit 1
        fi

        if [[ ! "$$ADMIN_PASSWORD" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_@.+-]+$$ ]]; then
          echo "Use letters, digits, or _ @ . + - in the administrator password." >&2
          exit 1
        fi

        # SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
        # Embedded in catalogue manifests that install a server through SteamCMD.
        # A package passes a dedicated-server app ID and either linux or windows.
        nex_steamcmd_update() {
          local app_id="$$1" platform="$$2"
          local archive attempt architecture steamclient
          local -a update=(+@ShutdownOnFailedCommand 1 +@NoPromptForPassword 1)

          cd "$$HOME"
          mkdir -p steamcmd serverfiles
          if [[ ! -x steamcmd/steamcmd.sh ]]; then
            archive=$$(mktemp)
            if ! curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \
              https://media.steampowered.com/client/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz -o "$$archive" \
              || ! tar -xzf "$$archive" -C steamcmd; then
              rm -f "$$archive"
              return 1
            fi
            rm -f "$$archive"
          fi

          if [[ "$$platform" == windows ]]; then
            update+=(+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows)
          fi
          update+=(+force_install_dir "$$HOME/serverfiles" +login anonymous +app_update "$$app_id" +quit)

          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh "$${update[@]}"; then
              break
            fi
            if [[ "$$attempt" == 3 ]]; then
              return 1
            fi
            sleep "$$((attempt * 5))"
          done

          for architecture in 32 64; do
            steamclient="$$HOME/steamcmd/linux$$architecture/steamclient.so"
            if [[ -f "$$steamclient" ]]; then
              mkdir -p ".steam/sdk$$architecture"
              ln -sfn "$$steamclient" ".steam/sdk$$architecture/steamclient.so"
            fi
          done
          cd serverfiles
        }


        nex_steamcmd_update 824360 windows

        export STEAM_COMPAT_CLIENT_INSTALL_PATH="$$HOME/.steam/steam"

        export STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH="$$STEAM_COMPAT_CLIENT_INSTALL_PATH/steamapps/compatdata/824360"

        mkdir -p "$$STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH"

        install_redistributable() (
          local stamp="$$STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH/$$1" url="$$2" stage status=0
          [[ ! -f "$$stamp" ]] || exit 0
          stage=$$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$$stage"' EXIT
          curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 "$$url" -o "$$stage/runtime.exe"
          timeout 10m xvfb-run -a -s "-nolisten tcp" proton run "$$stage/runtime.exe" /install /quiet /norestart || status=$$?
          # Windows exit code 3010 (restart requested) is truncated to 194 on Linux.
          if [[ "$$status" -ne 0 && "$$status" -ne 194 ]]; then
            echo "The Windows runtime installer exited with status $$status." >&2
            exit "$$status"
          fi
          touch "$$stamp"
        )
        install_redistributable .vcredist-x64-installed https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe

        install_redistributable .dotnet-desktop-6-x64-installed   https://builds.dotnet.microsoft.com/dotnet/WindowsDesktop/6.0.36/windowsdesktop-runtime-6.0.36-win-x64.exe

        install_steamworks() {
          local target="$$1"
          if [[ ! -f "$$target/steamclient64.dll" ]]; then
            "$$HOME/steamcmd/steamcmd.sh"       +@ShutdownOnFailedCommand 1 +@NoPromptForPassword 1 +@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows       +force_install_dir "$$target" +login anonymous +app_update 1007 +quit
            test -f "$$target/steamclient64.dll"
          fi
        }

        binary_dir="$$PWD/ShooterGame/Binaries/Win64"
        server="$$binary_dir/PixARKServer.exe"
        test -f "$$server"
        install_steamworks "$$binary_dir"
        world="CubeWorld_Light?listen?DelayRegisterServer=True?bRawSockets=True?SessionName=Nex PixARK?AltSaveDirectoryName=NexWorld?ServerPassword=$$JOIN_PASSWORD?ServerAdminPassword=$$ADMIN_PASSWORD?MaxPlayers=10?RCONEnabled=False"
        exec xvfb-run -a -s "-nolisten tcp" proton run "$$server" "$$world" \
          -Seed=12345 -OreSeed=1234 -ConfigsUseAltDir -server -gameplaylogging -log \
          -CULTUREFORCOOKING=en -NoBattlEye -QueryPort=27016 -Port=27015 -CubePort=27018 \
          -cubeworld=NexWorld -nosteamclient -NoHangDetection -Unattended -stdout -FullStdOutLogOutput
    stop_signal: SIGINT

  summary: Host a shared survival world in the wasteland
  description: >-

    Use the app’s Primary address on UDP 7777. UDP 27016 handles Steam discovery. Configure the world
    and access in serverfiles/configs/server.json after the first boot. SteamCMD downloads the server
    on first boot and checks for updates on restart. Allow time for the first download. Make a stopped
    backup before applying game updates.
  category: games
  website: https://store.steampowered.com/app/2218970/
  source: https://github.com/nexvirtualization/nex-catalogue/tree/main/apps/plains-of-pain

services:

    expose:
      - 7777/udp
      - 27016/udp
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/home/container
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    command:
      - /bin/bash
      - -ec
      - |
        # SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
        # Embedded in catalogue manifests that install a server through SteamCMD.
        # A package passes a dedicated-server app ID and either linux or windows.
        nex_steamcmd_update() {
          local app_id="$$1" platform="$$2"
          local archive attempt architecture steamclient
          local -a update=(+@ShutdownOnFailedCommand 1 +@NoPromptForPassword 1)

          cd "$$HOME"
          mkdir -p steamcmd serverfiles
          if [[ ! -x steamcmd/steamcmd.sh ]]; then
            archive=$$(mktemp)
            if ! curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \
              https://media.steampowered.com/client/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz -o "$$archive" \
              || ! tar -xzf "$$archive" -C steamcmd; then
              rm -f "$$archive"
              return 1
            fi
            rm -f "$$archive"
          fi

          if [[ "$$platform" == windows ]]; then
            update+=(+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows)
          fi
          update+=(+force_install_dir "$$HOME/serverfiles" +login anonymous +app_update "$$app_id" +quit)

          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh "$${update[@]}"; then
              break
            fi
            if [[ "$$attempt" == 3 ]]; then
              return 1
            fi
            sleep "$$((attempt * 5))"
          done

          for architecture in 32 64; do
            steamclient="$$HOME/steamcmd/linux$$architecture/steamclient.so"
            if [[ -f "$$steamclient" ]]; then
              mkdir -p ".steam/sdk$$architecture"
              ln -sfn "$$steamclient" ".steam/sdk$$architecture/steamclient.so"
            fi
          done
          cd serverfiles
        }

        nex_steamcmd_update 2227360 linux
        if [[ ! -e configs/server.json ]]; then
          cp configs/default.json configs/server.json
        fi
        exec ./PlainsOfPain.x86_64 -nographics -batchmode -ignorecompilererrors -cc -config configs/server.json -port 7777 -queryPort 27016

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: Puck
  summary: Host a physics-based multiplayer ice hockey server
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Use the app’s Primary address on TCP and UDP 30609. Use the join password you set at install.
    Keep automatic UPnP forwarding disabled at the network gateway. To change match settings or
    rotate the password later, edit server_config.json in the managed serverfiles folder and restart.
    SteamCMD downloads the server on first boot and checks for updates on restart. Allow time for the
    first download. Make a stopped backup before applying game updates.
  category: games
  website: https://store.steampowered.com/app/2994020/
  source: https://github.com/nexvirtualization/nex-catalogue/tree/main/apps/puck
  docs: https://steamcommunity.com/app/2994020/allnews/
  license: Proprietary game server
  architectures:
    - amd64
  tags:
    - steam
    - multiplayer
  options:
    JOIN_PASSWORD:
      label: Initial join password
      type: password
      help: Use 8 to 64 letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens.
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  puck:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/steamcmd:debian
    environment:
      JOIN_PASSWORD: ${JOIN_PASSWORD}
    expose:
      - 30609/tcp
      - 30609/udp
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/home/container
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    command:
      - /bin/bash
      - -ec
      - |
        # SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
        # Embedded in catalogue manifests that install a server through SteamCMD.
        # A package passes a dedicated-server app ID and either linux or windows.
        nex_steamcmd_update() {
          local app_id="$$1" platform="$$2"
          local archive attempt architecture steamclient
          local -a update=(+@ShutdownOnFailedCommand 1 +@NoPromptForPassword 1)

          cd "$$HOME"
          mkdir -p steamcmd serverfiles
          if [[ ! -x steamcmd/steamcmd.sh ]]; then
            archive=$$(mktemp)
            if ! curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \
              https://media.steampowered.com/client/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz -o "$$archive" \
              || ! tar -xzf "$$archive" -C steamcmd; then
              rm -f "$$archive"
              return 1
            fi
            rm -f "$$archive"
          fi

          if [[ "$$platform" == windows ]]; then
            update+=(+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows)
          fi
          update+=(+force_install_dir "$$HOME/serverfiles" +login anonymous +app_update "$$app_id" +quit)

          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh "$${update[@]}"; then
              break
            fi
            if [[ "$$attempt" == 3 ]]; then
              return 1
            fi
            sleep "$$((attempt * 5))"
          done

          for architecture in 32 64; do
            steamclient="$$HOME/steamcmd/linux$$architecture/steamclient.so"
            if [[ -f "$$steamclient" ]]; then
              mkdir -p ".steam/sdk$$architecture"
              ln -sfn "$$steamclient" ".steam/sdk$$architecture/steamclient.so"
            fi
          done
          cd serverfiles
        }

        if [[ ! "$$JOIN_PASSWORD" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$$ ]]; then
          echo 'Choose a join password with 8 to 64 letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens.' >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        nex_steamcmd_update 3481440 linux
        if [[ ! -e server_config.json ]]; then
          umask 077
          printf '{"port":30609,"name":"Nex Puck","maxPlayers":12,"password":"%s","tickRate":200,"isPublic":false,"useVoip":false,"useWhitelist":false,"mods":[],"gameMode":"public","level":"default"}\n' "$$JOIN_PASSWORD" > server_config.json
        fi
        # The server logs its JSON settings at startup. Retain the rest of the output.
        set -o pipefail
        ./start_server.sh 2>&1 | sed -uE 's/("password"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*")[^"]*/\1[redacted]/Ig'

  description: Connect CalDAV and CardDAV clients through an HTTPS proxy. The package manages the admin
    password from Nex and stores calendar collections in the application folder.
  category: productivity
  website: https://github.com/Kozea/Radicale

  docs: https://radicale.org/v3.html
  primary_service: radicale
  scalable: false
  license: GPL-3.0
  web:
    port: 5232
  options:
    ACCESS_PASSWORD:
      label: Dav access password
      type: password
      help: Use Nex Generate. Connect with the username admin.
    DATA:

      help: Radicale collection files and the authentication database.
    PORT:
      label: Web port
      help: Host-published TCP port. With a dedicated Primary network and host publishing off, use the

  radicale:
    image: ghcr.io/kozea/radicale:stable
    command:
    - 'umask 077

      printf ''%s

      '' "$$RADICALE_PASSWORD" | htpasswd -iBc /var/lib/radicale/nex-htpasswd admin

      unset RADICALE_PASSWORD

      exec /app/bin/radicale --hosts 0.0.0.0:5232 --auth-type htpasswd --auth-htpasswd-filename /var/lib/radicale/nex-htpasswd
      --auth-htpasswd-encryption bcrypt --storage-filesystem-folder /var/lib/radicale/collections'
    entrypoint:
    - /bin/sh
    - -ec
    environment:

    volumes:
    - ${DATA}:/var/lib/radicale
    ports:
    - ${PORT:-5232}:5232/tcp
    deploy:

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: RimWorld Open World
  version: '1.0.4'
  summary: Host a shared world for the legacy Open World mod
  description: >-
    Keep the world files on This host and choose a registered primary network limited to your
    players. Use RimWorld 1.4 and the Open World mod on each client. The server expects Open World
    client version 1.3. Connect to the app’s Primary address on TCP 25555. Configure server
    access in Data/Config.json before inviting players. Make a stopped backup before updating.
  category: games
  website: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2954574797
  source: https://github.com/D12-Dev/OpenWorld
  docs: https://github.com/D12-Dev/OpenWorld#quick-installation-guide
  license: CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0
  architectures: [amd64, arm64]
  tags: [multiplayer, simulation]
  options:
    DATA:
      label: World, player saves and server settings
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  rimworld-open-world:
    image: ghcr.io/ptero-eggs/yolks:dotnet_10
    working_dir: /data
    user: '0:0'
    entrypoint: [/usr/bin/tini, -g, --, /bin/sh, -ec]
    command:
      - |
        umask 027
        chown container:container /data
        if [ ! -f .open-world-installed-1.0.4 ] || [ ! -s OpenWorldServer.dll ]; then
          case "$$(uname -m)" in
            x86_64)
              archive=linux-x64
              sha256=dba0571b82ea2df2762d1b7640d58ee64be1290d0b22248d606c729ac1347d22
              ;;
            aarch64)
              archive=linux-arm64
              sha256=4065b0ef91f429901eae69dbee8756fc2283617f081e162c21b56dbe15e3966e
              ;;
            *)
              echo 'RimWorld Open World requires amd64 or arm64.' >&2
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac
          stage=$$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$$stage"' EXIT
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$$stage/server.zip" "https://github.com/D12-Dev/OpenWorld/releases/download/v1.0.4/$$archive.zip"
          printf '%s  %s\n' "$$sha256" "$$stage/server.zip" | sha256sum -c -
          unzip -q "$$stage/server.zip" -d "$$stage"
          install -o container -g container -m 0644 "$$stage/$$archive"/*.dll "$$stage/$$archive"/*.json /data/
          touch .open-world-installed-1.0.4
          rm -rf "$$stage"
          trap - EXIT
        fi
        exec setpriv --reuid=container --regid=container --init-groups dotnet OpenWorldServer.dll
    environment:
      DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD: LatestMajor
    expose:
      - 25555/tcp
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/data
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

      - |
        # SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
        # Embedded in catalogue manifests that install a server through SteamCMD.
        # A package passes a dedicated-server app ID and either linux or windows.
        nex_steamcmd_update() {
          local app_id="$$1" platform="$$2"
          local archive attempt architecture steamclient
          local -a update=(+@ShutdownOnFailedCommand 1 +@NoPromptForPassword 1)

          cd "$$HOME"
          mkdir -p steamcmd serverfiles
          if [[ ! -x steamcmd/steamcmd.sh ]]; then
            archive=$$(mktemp)
            if ! curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \
              https://media.steampowered.com/client/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz -o "$$archive" \
              || ! tar -xzf "$$archive" -C steamcmd; then
              rm -f "$$archive"
              return 1
            fi
            rm -f "$$archive"
          fi

          if [[ "$$platform" == windows ]]; then
            update+=(+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows)
          fi
          update+=(+force_install_dir "$$HOME/serverfiles" +login anonymous +app_update "$$app_id" +quit)

          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if ./steamcmd/steamcmd.sh "$${update[@]}"; then

            fi
            if [[ "$$attempt" == 3 ]]; then

            fi
          done
          cd serverfiles
        }

        nex_steamcmd_update 1086950 linux
        exec "./Solace Crafting.x86_64" -batchmode -nographics -logFile -

            archive=$$(mktemp)
            if ! curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --retry 3 \

              || ! tar -xzf "$$archive" -C steamcmd; then
              rm -f "$$archive"
              return 1
            fi
            rm -f "$$archive"
          fi

          if [[ "$$platform" == windows ]]; then
            update+=(+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows)
          fi
          update+=(+force_install_dir "$$HOME/serverfiles" +login anonymous +app_update "$$app_id" +quit)

          for attempt in 1 2 3; do

            if [[ "$$attempt" == 3 ]]; then
              return 1
            fi
            sleep "$$((attempt * 5))"
          done

          for architecture in 32 64; do
            steamclient="$$HOME/steamcmd/linux$$architecture/steamclient.so"
            if [[ -f "$$steamclient" ]]; then

              ln -sfn "$$steamclient" ".steam/sdk$$architecture/steamclient.so"

        }

        nex_steamcmd_update 638500 linux

  summary: Build a shared industrial base on Arcadia-7
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    First boot downloads the dedicated server and creates a new session. Join from Multiplayer with
    the app’s Primary address on UDP 7777. Once a save exists, turn off Create world and restart the
    app to load the saved session. The in-game management interface is disabled. Make a stopped backup
    before applying game updates.
  category: games
  website: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1631270/
  source: https://github.com/indifferentbroccoli/starrupture-server-docker
  docs: https://github.com/indifferentbroccoli/starrupture-server-docker#readme
  license: Proprietary game server
  architectures:
    - amd64
  tags:
    - survival
    - co-op
    - steam
  options:
    NEW_WORLD:
      label: Create world
      type: bool
      help: Enable this on first boot. Disable it once the first save exists.
    JOIN_PASSWORD:
      label: Join password
      type: password
      help: Use letters, digits, or _ @ . + -.
    ADMIN_PASSWORD:
      label: Administrator password
      type: password
      help: Use letters, digits, or _ @ . + -.
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  starrupture:
    image: docker.io/indifferentbroccoli/starrupture-server-docker:latest
    environment:
      PUID: '1000'
      PGID: '1000'
      SERVER_NAME: Nex StarRupture
      DEFAULT_PORT: '7777'
      USE_DSSETTINGS: 'true'
      START_NEW_GAME: ${NEW_WORLD}
      NEW_WORLD: ${NEW_WORLD}
      ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      PLAYER_PASSWORD: ${JOIN_PASSWORD}
      JOIN_PASSWORD: ${JOIN_PASSWORD}
      UPDATE_ON_START: 'true'
    expose:
      - 7777/udp
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/home/steam/server-files
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    entrypoint:
      - /bin/bash
      - -ec
      - |
        if [[ ! "$${JOIN_PASSWORD}" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_@.+-]+$$ ||
              ! "$${ADMIN_PASSWORD}" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_@.+-]+$$ ]]; then
          echo "Use letters, numbers or _ @ . + - in both passwords." >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        if [ "$$NEW_WORLD" = true ]; then
          export LOAD_SAVED_GAME=false
        else
          export LOAD_SAVED_GAME=true
        fi
        exec /home/steam/server/init.sh

    backups and server logs as private because they can contain Steam server credentials.
  category: games
  website: https://store.steampowered.com/app/440/

  docs: https://linuxgsm.com/servers/tf2server/

  architectures: [amd64]

    - multiplayer

      label: Steam game server login token
      type: password

services:
  team-fortress-2:
    image: ghcr.io/gameservermanagers/gameserver:tf2
    entrypoint:
      - /bin/bash
      - -ec
      - |

      UPDATE_ON_START: "true"

      - "27015/udp"
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/data
    healthcheck:
      start_period: 25m
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

    STEAMCMD:
      label: SteamCMD cache
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  the-forest:
    image: ghcr.io/ich777/steamcmd:theforest
    environment:
      GAME_ID: '556450'
      GAME_PARAMS: ''
      JOIN_PASSWORD: ${JOIN_PASSWORD}
      ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${ADMIN_PASSWORD}
    expose:
      - 8766/udp
      - 27015/udp
      - 27016/udp
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/serverdata/serverfiles
      - ${STEAMCMD}:/serverdata/steamcmd
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    entrypoint:
      - /bin/bash
      - -ec
      - |
        if [[ ! "$${JOIN_PASSWORD}" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_@.+-]+$$ ||
              ! "$${ADMIN_PASSWORD}" =~ ^[a-zA-Z0-9_@.+-]+$$ ]]; then
          echo "Use letters, numbers or _ @ . + - in both passwords." >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        config=/serverdata/serverfiles/config/config.cfg
        if [ ! -e "$$config" ]; then
          mkdir -p "$${config%/*}"
          umask 077
          cat > "$$config" <<EOF
        serverIP 0.0.0.0
        serverSteamPort 8766
        serverGamePort 27015
        serverQueryPort 27016
        serverName Nex The Forest
        serverPlayers 8
        serverPassword $$JOIN_PASSWORD
        serverPasswordAdmin $$ADMIN_PASSWORD
        serverAutoSaveInterval 30
        difficulty Normal
        initType Continue
        slot 1
        allowCheats off
        EOF
        fi
        exec /opt/scripts/start.sh

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: Trackmania
  summary: Host a dedicated racing room
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Register a dedicated-server account with Ubisoft at players.trackmania.com/server/dedicated and
    provide its login and password in Nex. Find the server in the Trackmania multiplayer browser.
    The server uses TCP and UDP 2350. Match settings and tracks are in the managed folder. Make a
    stopped backup before applying game updates.
  category: games
  website: https://store.steampowered.com/app/2225070/
  source: https://github.com/EvoEsports/docker-trackmania
  docs: https://github.com/EvoEsports/docker-trackmania#readme
  license: Proprietary game server
  architectures:
    - amd64
  tags:
    - racing
    - multiplayer
  options:
    MASTER_LOGIN:
      label: Dedicated-server login
      help: Enter the login of the dedicated-server account.
    MASTER_PASSWORD:
      label: Dedicated-server password
      type: password
      help: Enter the password for that account.
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  trackmania:
    image: docker.io/evoesports/trackmania:latest
    environment:
      MASTER_LOGIN: ${MASTER_LOGIN}
      MASTER_PASSWORD: ${MASTER_PASSWORD}
    expose:
      - 2350/tcp
      - 2350/udp
    volumes:
      - ${DATA}:/data
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
    entrypoint:
      - /bin/bash
      - -ec
      - |
        if [[ -z "$$MASTER_LOGIN" || -z "$$MASTER_PASSWORD" ]]; then
          echo "Enter your Trackmania dedicated-server login and password." >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        if [ ! -L /server/UserData ]; then
          cp -an /server/UserData/. /data/
          mv /server/UserData /server/UserData.defaults
          ln -s /data /server/UserData
        fi
        config=/data/Config/nex-dedicated.cfg
        if [ ! -f "$$config" ]; then
          cp /data/Config/dedicated_cfg.default.txt "$$config"
        fi
        if [ ! -f /data/Maps/MatchSettings/default.txt ]; then
          cp /data/Maps/MatchSettings/example.txt /data/Maps/MatchSettings/default.txt
        fi
        xmlstarlet ed -L \
          -u '/dedicated/masterserver_account/login' -v "$$MASTER_LOGIN" \
          -u '/dedicated/masterserver_account/password' -v "$$MASTER_PASSWORD" \
          -u '/dedicated/system_config/server_port' -v '2350' \
          -u '/dedicated/system_config/xmlrpc_allowremote' -v 'False' \
          -u '/dedicated/server_options/name' -v 'Nex Trackmania' "$$config"
        chmod 0600 "$$config"
        chown -R trackmania:trackmania /data
        exec su-exec trackmania ./TrackmaniaServer /dedicated_cfg=nex-dedicated.cfg \
          /game_settings=MatchSettings/default.txt /noDaemon
    user: "0:0"

x-nex:
  name: WriteFreely
  summary: Publish a Markdown blog or writing community
  description: Runs a standalone SQLite instance with dedicated storage for the configuration, database and keys.
    Prepare config.ini in the State folder before installing. The app initializes a new SQLite instance on startup.
  category: productivity
  website: https://writefreely.org/
  source: https://github.com/writefreely/writefreely
  docs: https://writefreely.org/docs/latest/admin/config
  license: AGPL-3.0-only
  primary_service: writefreely
  web:
    port: 8080
  options:
    STATE:
      label: State folder
      help: Use a writable folder on This host with config.ini at its root. Configure the sqlite3 database
        filename as /data/writefreely.db, leave keys_parent_dir at its default, and set server bind to
        0.0.0.0 and port to 8080.
    KEYS:
      label: Encryption keys
      help: Keep on This host and back up with State. Retain these keys when moving an existing installation.
    PORT:
      label: Web port
      help: Host port for the listener on 8080 when host publishing is available.
  post_install: >-
    Disable open registration in config.ini until you are ready. Inside the container, run
    `/go/cmd/writefreely/writefreely -c /data/config.ini --create-admin 'USERNAME:PASSWORD'`
    with your own administrator credentials, then open the web interface.
services:
  writefreely:
    image: ghcr.io/writefreely/writefreely:v0.17.1
    working_dir: /go
    entrypoint: [/bin/sh, -ec]
    command:
      - |
        if [ ! -r /data/config.ini ]; then
          echo "Prepare /data/config.ini before starting WriteFreely" >&2
          exit 1
        fi
        if [ ! -s /data/writefreely.db ]; then
          if [ -z "$$(ls -A /go/keys | grep -v -e README.md -e .gitkeep || true)" ]; then
            /go/cmd/writefreely/writefreely -c /data/config.ini --gen-keys
          fi
          /go/cmd/writefreely/writefreely -c /data/config.ini --init-db
        fi
        exec /go/cmd/writefreely/writefreely -c /data/config.ini
    volumes:
      - ${STATE}:/data
      - ${KEYS}:/go/keys
    ports:
      - ${PORT:-19430}:8080/tcp
    deploy:
      replicas: 1

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-only
x-nex:
  name: Zandronum
  summary: Host multiplayer Doom-compatible maps with Freedoom
  description: >-
    Keep the game folders on This host and choose a registered primary network that players can reach.
    Direct connect using Zandronum 3.2.1 or Doomseeker to the app’s Primary address on UDP 10666. Use
    Freedoom Phase 2 as the base game. At first start the app downloads the verified Zandronum release
    and Freedoom data. Stop the app before editing server.cfg in the managed folder.
  category: games
  website: https://zandronum.com/
  source: https://github.com/ich777/docker-zandronum
  docs: https://zandronum.com/download
  license: Zandronum with free Freedoom game data
  architectures:
  - amd64
  tags:
  - fps
  - multiplayer
  options:
    DATA:
      label: Server data
      help: Choose This host and include this folder in stopped backups.
services:
  zandronum:
    image: ghcr.io/ich777/zandronum:latest
    expose:
    - 10666/udp
    volumes:
    - ${DATA}:/zandronum
    user: 1000:1000
    entrypoint:
    - /bin/bash
    - -ec
    - |
      cd /zandronum
      mkdir -p wads
      if [ ! -x ./zandronum-server ] || [ ! -f ./wads/freedoom2.wad ]; then
        staging=$$(mktemp -d ./.zandronum-install.XXXXXX)
        trap 'rm -rf "$$staging"' EXIT
        if [ ! -x ./zandronum-server ]; then
          wget -q -O "$$staging/server.tar.bz2" https://zandronum.com/downloads/zandronum3.2.1-linux-x86_64.tar.bz2
          printf '%s  %s\n' 9f4b93ed99ab15d2406e697e2a06d956eb808c9ac2e53e62ae9f1affb53c86c0 "$$staging/server.tar.bz2" | sha256sum -c --status
          tar -xjf "$$staging/server.tar.bz2" -C "$$staging" zandronum-server zandronum.pk3 skulltag_actors.pk3
          mv "$$staging/zandronum.pk3" "$$staging/skulltag_actors.pk3" ./
          chmod 755 "$$staging/zandronum-server"
          mv "$$staging/zandronum-server" ./
        fi
        if [ ! -f ./wads/freedoom2.wad ]; then
          wget -q -O "$$staging/freedoom.deb" https://deb.debian.org/debian/pool/main/f/freedoom/freedoom_0.13.0-3_all.deb
          printf '%s  %s\n' 6b08208c081a4ab8958c3790c29db7abdf3dfe61ad913ddcb4d91b4e0c58c2f6 "$$staging/freedoom.deb" | sha256sum -c --status
          dpkg-deb -x "$$staging/freedoom.deb" "$$staging/freedoom"
          mv "$$staging/freedoom/usr/share/games/doom/freedoom2.wad" ./wads/freedoom2.wad
        fi
        rm -rf "$$staging"
        trap - EXIT
      fi
      if [ ! -f ./server.cfg ]; then
        printf 'sv_hostname "Nex Zandronum"\nsv_rconpassword ""\nsv_updatemaster false\n' > ./server.cfg
      fi
      exec ./zandronum-server -host 8 -port 10666 -iwad ./wads/freedoom2.wad -exec ./server.cfg
    stop_grace_period: 90s
    deploy:
      replicas: 1
